He became president in September 1901 following the assassination of William McKinley , making him the youngest person to hold the office at the time. He subsequently won election in his own right in 1904.

As president, Roosevelt pursued an active approach to government. His administration took on powerful corporate interests, supported consumer protections and advanced conservation efforts.

The National Park Service credits his conservation legacy with protecting more than 230 million acres of public land through national forests, monuments and other federal designations.

His career involved decisions with consequences far beyond his own circumstances.

Although the quote about accepting a job is not necessarily an original Roosevelt saying, its emphasis on action and practical problem-solving fits the public image he cultivated throughout his life.

Roosevelt's record also illustrates that action does not guarantee an easy path or an immediate victory. Leadership involves making decisions with incomplete information, learning from setbacks and remaining accountable for the results.

In an age when professional opportunities can require people to adapt quickly, Roosevelt's associated maxim still resonates. Employers value initiative, while many careers demand continuous learning as technology and working practices evolve.

The saying offers encouragement to people who hesitate because they believe they must be completely prepared before attempting something new.

Often, the first step is to recognise that a challenge is possible, followed by the disciplined effort needed to make it happen.

Ultimately, the lesson is not that everyone should claim to be capable of everything. It is that uncertainty does not always have to be the end of an opportunity.

With preparation, curiosity, persistence and the willingness to ask for help, unfamiliar responsibilities can become opportunities for growth.

That is the practical wisdom behind the quotation attributed to Theodore Roosevelt: confidence may open the door, but effort, learning and accountability are what allow someone to walk through it.

articles.title: Powerball Winning Numbers: Results for Wednesday, October 28 drawing for the $716 million jackpot
articles.standfirst: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $716 million
articles.summary: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $716 million
articles.body:
Lottery players are hoping to land a life-changing prize as Powerball prepares for its Wednesday, October 28, 2026 drawing. The jackpot has reached an estimated $716 million after another drawing ended without a ticket matching all six numbers.

The winning numbers for October 28 have not yet been announced. The draw is scheduled for 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time, and players should check the official Powerball website after the results are released to confirm the numbers and prize information.

The jackpot has continued to grow since the previous top prize was claimed in August. Monday's drawing, held on October 26, did not produce a jackpot winner, meaning the potential reward has increased for the latest opportunity.

The advertised $716 million figure represents the estimated annuity prize, paid through a series of annual instalments. Winners who prefer to receive their money in a single payment can instead select the estimated cash option of $307.2 million, before taxes.

Previous Powerball results and what players need to know

The most recent completed drawing took place on Monday, October 26. Its winning numbers were 18, 26, 49, 50 and 54, with Powerball 1. The Power Play multiplier was 3x.

Although nobody secured the jackpot, two tickets sold in Florida and Georgia matched all five white balls, earning $1 million each. Those prizes demonstrate that substantial winnings remain possible even without matching the red Powerball number.

Wednesday's draw gives players another opportunity to match the five white balls and the separate red Powerball . The numbers are selected independently, and previous results do not make particular numbers more likely to appear in a future drawing.

The jackpot's size has attracted additional attention, but the odds of winning the top prize remain extremely long.

According to Powerball , the odds of matching all five white balls and the Powerball are approximately 1 in 292.2 million. The overall odds of winning any prize are considerably better, at approximately 1 in 24.9.

How much could the winner actually receive?

The headline jackpot is not necessarily the amount a winner would take home. The annuity option distributes the prize over 30 payments: one initial payment followed by 29 annual payments that increase over time. The cash option provides a smaller amount upfront instead.

Taxes also affect the final payout. Federal withholding applies to large lottery prizes, and the winner's final federal tax liability may be higher than the amount initially withheld. State and local taxes can reduce the prize further, depending on where the winning ticket was purchased and the winner's circumstances.

For that reason, the $716 million figure should be understood as the advertised annuity value rather than a guaranteed lump-sum payment.

Where to check Wednesday's winning numbers

Players can visit the official Powerball website to find the winning numbers once the drawing has concluded. The website also provides previous results, prize details and information about the next scheduled drawing.

Powerball drawings normally take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday at 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

Ticket-sale deadlines vary by state and jurisdiction, so players should check their local lottery's rules for cutoff times and prize-claim procedures.

Anyone checking a ticket should compare all five white-ball numbers and the red Powerball against the official results, while also checking the Power Play selection if they purchased that option. Tickets should be retained until the result has been verified and any applicable claim instructions reviewed.

With $716 million at stake, Wednesday's drawing is attracting considerable interest. However, until the draw takes place and the official results are published, the October 28 winning numbers remain unknown.

This article will be updated once the confirmed numbers and prize breakdown become available.

articles.title: Great white shark lunges at woman after she tries to pet it like a dog during fishing trip
articles.summary: What happens when you try to pet a great white shark like it's your family dog? Well, this woman found out!
articles.body:
What happens when you try to pet a great white shark like it's your family dog? Well, this woman found out!

During a fishing trip off the coast of Georgia, a woman named Jen reached over the side of a boat to stroke the shark's head.

But the massive predator suddenly lunged, slamming its mouth against the boat!

Luckily, nobody was hurt. The crew said the shark was under control and the woman was never in real danger.

During a fishing trip off the coast of Georgia, a woman named Jen reached over the side of a boat to stroke the shark's head.
But the massive predator suddenly lunged, slamming its mouth against the boat!
Luckily, nobody was hurt. The crew said the shark was under control and the woman was never in real danger.

articles.title: Costco November Discounts: Deals, coupons and everything you can get for next month
articles.standfirst: Two overlapping promotions are bringing new savings to Costco members, but some offers expire before Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Two overlapping promotions are bringing new savings to Costco members, but some offers expire before Thanksgiving
articles.body:
The holiday shopping season is arriving early at Costco , where a new collection of discounts is giving members the chance to stock up on everyday essentials before Thanksgiving and the busy Christmas period.

Rather than relying on a single Black Friday sale, the warehouse retailer is running overlapping promotions throughout November, creating different opportunities to save depending on when customers shop.

Its latest members-only coupon book began on October 19 and runs until November 15, featuring reductions on cleaning supplies, toiletries, food and baking ingredients.

Meanwhile, Costco 's separate Holiday Savings event begins October 30 and continues through November 30, although individual offers may be available for shorter periods.

That distinction matters because customers waiting until Black Friday itself could miss discounts included in the regular November promotion.

Some of the most practical offers involve products that households regularly purchase, particularly those looking to prepare for holiday guests.

Costco is offering $4.50 off 16-packs of Dove Moisturizing Beauty Bars, while Listerine UltraClean Cool Mint Mouthwash is reduced by $4 for a package containing two 1.5-liter bottles.

Laundry supplies are also included, with $6 off Tide + Ultra Oxi Powder Detergent, sold in a 225-ounce container designed to provide approximately 143 loads.

In the kitchen, customers can save $7 on Reynolds Wrap Everyday Aluminum Foil, which comes with two 250-square-foot rolls.

Another potentially useful holiday purchase is Kirkland Signature Alkaline Batteries, with $2 off 48-count packs of AA or AAA batteries.

These offers are available under Costco 's October 19 to November 15 savings period, subject to availability and applicable purchasing conditions.

Holiday groceries and baking essentials

The promotion also offers useful savings for anyone planning Thanksgiving meals or preparing for Christmas entertaining.

Nielsen-Massey Madagascar Bourbon Pure Vanilla Extract is among the larger reductions, with $15 off a package containing two eight-ounce bottles.

Shoppers can also save $3.30 on an 18-stack box of Nabisco Ritz Crackers and $2.70 on a three-pack of Boursin Gourmet Cheese.

The cheese selection includes two Garlic & Fine Herbs varieties and one Shallot & Chive, making it a convenient addition to holiday appetizers.

Pet owners can also take advantage of $5 off a two-pound package of Bocce's Bakery Duck & Blueberry dog treats.

These reductions provide opportunities to buy products ahead of seasonal demand without waiting for Black Friday itself.

When Costco Black Friday 2026 deals start and end

The separate Holiday Savings event begins October 30 and runs through November 30, with different products discounted at different stages of the promotion.

Costco 's advertised offers include savings on selected electronics, home appliances and jewelry, alongside seasonal grocery products. The retailer is also promoting discounts on laptops, televisions and refrigerators.

Members should review individual promotional dates because an item advertised as part of Holiday Savings may not remain discounted throughout November.

Costco will also close its US warehouses on Thanksgiving Day, Thursday, November 26, making it important to plan shopping trips accordingly.

Customers can check availability and prices through Costco's website or mobile app, although warehouse and online pricing may differ.

The retailer's members-only savings generally require no additional coupon codes, with eligible discounts reflected in the advertised prices.

With two overlapping sales running through November, the best approach is to identify which products are needed and check when their respective discounts expire.

Shoppers seeking everyday household savings have until November 15 to use the current coupon book, while those looking for larger holiday purchases will have additional opportunities throughout the Black Friday promotion.

articles.title: A possible new dwarf planet appears beyond Pluto: what is known about 2026 ED138
articles.standfirst: Astronomers found a dwarf planet on the outskirts of the solar system, beyond Pluto, thanks to the newly inaugurated Vera Rubin Observatory in Chile.
articles.summary: Astronomers found a dwarf planet on the outskirts of the solar system, beyond Pluto, thanks to the newly inaugurated Vera Rubin Observatory in Chile.
articles.body:
The Solar System could have a new member on its official list of dwarf planets. Scientists identified a large icy object orbiting beyond Pluto that, based on its preliminary characteristics, could become one of the largest bodies in this category known so far.

The object, provisionally designated 2026 ED138, was detected thanks to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, located on Cerro Pachón, Chile. Initial calculations place its diameter at between approximately 600 and 1,500 kilometers, although astronomers still need to determine its size more precisely before officially establishing its nature.

2026 ED138 is even farther from the Sun than Pluto

According to the researchers, the new planet, is currently located at a distance from the Sun equivalent to about 46 times the separation between the Earth and our star. By comparison, Pluto orbits at an average distance close to 40 times the one separating the Earth from the Sun.

The discovery was made possible thanks to Rubin's ability to continuously observe large expanses of the sky . The object was located in an area near the plane of the Milky Way, filled with millions of stars, a circumstance that would previously have made its detection difficult. The observatory's systems were able to identify its movement against that enormous stellar background.

Matt Holman, an astrophysicist at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian and the one who identified the object, stated that the discovery shows that there are still numerous bodies yet to be found in the most distant regions of the Solar System. The next step will be to establish the physical size of ED138 with greater precision.

The main thing we need to do is establish the physical size of 2026 ED138

What is missing for it to be considered a dwarf planet?

To officially receive that classification, a body must have enough mass for its own gravity to give it an approximately spherical shape.

Available data indicate that 2026 ED138 could meet that condition, but scientists still do not have the measurements needed to confirm it.

One of the problems is that Rubin mainly observes sunlight reflected by the object.

A small but highly reflective body can appear as bright as a larger one with a darker surface. That is why researchers hope to turn to observations at other wavelengths, including the possibility of using ALMA, also located in Chile, to better understand its dimensions.

If it is ultimately classified as a dwarf planet, 2026 ED138 would join the five currently recognized by the International Astronomical Union: Ceres, Pluto, Haumea, Makemake, and Eris. Pluto was part of the list of planets in the Solar System for decades until it was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

The discovery also reinforces expectations surrounding the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which began revealing thousands of new Solar System objects during 2026.

In April alone, the observatory reported data corresponding to more than 11,000 new asteroids, a sample of the potential of its observations to discover bodies that had until now gone unnoticed.

articles.title: What time will sunset be after this weekend's Daylight Savings ending for 2026 and everything you need to know about it?
articles.standfirst: Millions of Americans will notice darkness arriving much earlier this weekend as clocks move back one hour
articles.summary: Millions of Americans will notice darkness arriving much earlier this weekend as clocks move back one hour
articles.body:
The sun will disappear below the horizon noticeably earlier across much of the United States this weekend, with the end of daylight saving time bringing an abrupt change to evening routines.

On Sunday, November 1, 2026, Americans in most states will turn their clocks back one hour, shifting the country from daylight saving time to standard time.

Although the adjustment provides an additional hour overnight, it also means sunset will occur approximately 60 minutes earlier according to the clock.

The difference will be especially noticeable in northern cities, where shorter autumn days are already reducing the amount of natural light available after work and school.

New York, Chicago, Boston and Seattle will all experience sunsets before 5 p.m. on Sunday, while southern cities such as Miami and Houston will retain more evening daylight.

What time will sunset be on November 1, 2026?

The precise time depends on geographic location, with northern areas generally experiencing shorter days as winter approaches.

Here are the approximate local sunset times for major US cities on Sunday, November 1.

The change will be particularly striking in northern Maine, where sunset in Caribou is expected at approximately 4:16 p.m.

In contrast, southern locations will continue enjoying daylight later into the afternoon, although they will still experience the one-hour clock adjustment.

When do clocks go back in the United States?

Daylight saving time officially ends at 2 a.m. local time on Sunday, November 1, when clocks move backward to 1 a.m.

That means the hour between 1 a.m. and 2 a.m. occurs twice, giving most Americans an additional hour overnight.

Smartphones, computers and other connected devices generally update automatically, while traditional clocks and certain household appliances may require manual changes.

Not every state participates, however. Hawaii and most of Arizona remain on standard time throughout the year, with the Navajo Nation observing daylight saving time as an exception.

Why will it get darker even earlier throughout November?

The clock change doesn't alter the actual amount of daylight, but the Northern Hemisphere will continue experiencing shorter days as winter approaches.

Daylight hours have gradually decreased since the summer solstice in June, with the trend continuing until the winter solstice on December 21.

Seattle, for example, is expected to lose more than 70 minutes of daylight between the beginning and end of November.

The decrease will be less substantial in southern states, where changes in daylight duration are smaller throughout the year.

Despite the earlier sunsets, Americans can expect brighter mornings immediately after the clock change.

Daylight saving time will begin again on Sunday, March 14, 2027 , when clocks move forward one hour and evening daylight returns later according to the clock.

On Sunday, November 1, 2026, Americans in most states will turn their clocks back one hour, shifting the country from daylight saving time to standard time.
Although the adjustment provides an additional hour overnight, it also means sunset will occur approximately 60 minutes earlier according to the clock.
The difference will be especially noticeable in northern cities, where shorter autumn days are already reducing the amount of natural light available after work and school.
New York, Chicago, Boston and Seattle will all experience sunsets before 5 p.m. on Sunday, while southern cities such as Miami and Houston will retain more evening daylight.
What time will sunset be on November 1, 2026?
The precise time depends on geographic location, with northern areas generally experiencing shorter days as winter approaches.
Here are the approximate local sunset times for major US cities on Sunday, November 1.
The change will be particularly striking in northern Maine, where sunset in Caribou is expected at approximately 4:16 p.m.
In contrast, southern locations will continue enjoying daylight later into the afternoon, although they will still experience the one-hour clock adjustment.
When do clocks go back in the United States?
Daylight saving time officially ends at 2 a.m. local time on Sunday, November 1, when clocks move backward to 1 a.m.
That means the hour between 1 a.m. and 2 a.m. occurs twice, giving most Americans an additional hour overnight.
Smartphones, computers and other connected devices generally update automatically, while traditional clocks and certain household appliances may require manual changes.
Not every state participates, however. Hawaii and most of Arizona remain on standard time throughout the year, with the Navajo Nation observing daylight saving time as an exception.
Why will it get darker even earlier throughout November?
The clock change doesn't alter the actual amount of daylight, but the Northern Hemisphere will continue experiencing shorter days as winter approaches.
Daylight hours have gradually decreased since the summer solstice in June, with the trend continuing until the winter solstice on December 21.
Seattle, for example, is expected to lose more than 70 minutes of daylight between the beginning and end of November.
The decrease will be less substantial in southern states, where changes in daylight duration are smaller throughout the year.
Despite the earlier sunsets, Americans can expect brighter mornings immediately after the clock change.
Daylight saving time will begin again on Sunday, March 14, 2027 , when clocks move forward one hour and evening daylight returns later according to the clock.

articles.title: How are the polls looking for the 2026 Midterm Elections and what are the key races that you must follow?
articles.standfirst: New polling reveals a significant Democratic lead while closely contested races in Ohio, Texas and Maine remain decisive
articles.summary: New polling reveals a significant Democratic lead while closely contested races in Ohio, Texas and Maine remain decisive
articles.body:
The battle for control of Congress is entering its final days with Democrats holding a clear advantage in national polling, although the Republican Party still has opportunities to protect its position in the Senate.

With Election Day scheduled for Tuesday, November 3, the latest PBS News/NPR/Marist survey places Democratic congressional candidates eight percentage points ahead of Republicans among likely voters.

The poll, conducted October 19-20, found that 52% would support the Democratic candidate in their district, compared with 44% backing the Republican.

Independent voters favor Democrats by 13 points, while the opposition party also holds an advantage in voter enthusiasm.

However, national polling doesn't necessarily translate directly into congressional seats, particularly in a political system where individual state contests and district boundaries can significantly influence the outcome.

What do the latest 2026 Midterm Election polls show?

The Marist survey found that 71% of Democratic likely voters were very enthusiastic about participating, compared with 61% of Republicans.

President Donald Trump is also an important factor, with 40% of likely voters approving of his performance and 59% disapproving.

Meanwhile, 44% described their congressional ballot as primarily a vote against Trump , compared with 21% who considered it a vote supporting him.

However, Republican strategist Melik Abdul cautioned against assuming the national polling advantage would produce an overwhelming Democratic victory.

"I don't think it will be the blue wave that people are suspecting," Abdul said.

The economy remains central to voters' decisions, with 34% identifying the cost of living as their leading concern and 33% prioritizing preserving democracy.

Which Senate races could decide 2026 Midterms?

The contest for the Senate remains particularly competitive, with several closely watched states potentially determining which party controls the chamber.

In Ohio, Republican Jon Husted faces former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown , while Texas features a contest between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico .

Maine is another major battleground, where Republican senator Susan Collins faces Democratic challenger Janet Mills .

Other important contests include Alaska, Michigan, Iowa, Kansas and North Carolina , where relatively small changes in turnout could prove decisive.

North Carolina's race features former Democratic governor Roy Cooper against Republican Michael Whatley , making it another closely watched contest.

The Senate remains a more difficult challenge for Democrats than the House because they must gain four seats to secure control, assuming no other changes to the chamber's composition.

What could determine control of the House of Representatives?

The House presents a different electoral challenge, with Republicans defending a narrow majority and dozens of competitive districts across the country.

Democratic strategist Joel Payne believes the party's national polling position is encouraging, although he acknowledged that individual contests remain important.

"The House feels fairly settled for Democrats," Payne said.

However, Republicans are concentrating on mobilizing supporters in districts where voter participation could outweigh the national polling trend.

More than 30 million Americans have already voted, according to figures cited by the University of Florida Election Lab, adding another dimension to the final campaign push.

The central question heading into November 3 is whether Democratic enthusiasm translates into sufficient victories across competitive districts and states, or whether Republican turnout allows the party to maintain control of one or both chambers.

articles.title: Tennessee governor clarifies Christa Pike's situation: "Surviving an execution does not cancel your death sentence"
articles.standfirst: Bill Lee says Christa Pike's death sentence is expected to remain in place following September's failed lethal-injection attempt
articles.summary: Bill Lee says Christa Pike's death sentence is expected to remain in place following September's failed lethal-injection attempt
articles.body:
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has addressed the future of Christa Pike following the extraordinary failure of the state's attempt to execute her, indicating that surviving the procedure will not automatically spare her from the death penalty.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, October 28, Lee was asked whether Tennessee would make another attempt to execute Pike or consider changing her punishment to life imprisonment.

His response suggested that any significant change to her sentence would depend on a decision by the courts.

"I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless determined otherwise by the courts,” Lee said.

The governor's comments come almost a month after Pike survived a lethal injection at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville on September 30. The 50-year-old was administered two doses of pentobarbital but remained alive, prompting emergency medical intervention and a hospital transfer.

The incident has raised serious questions about Tennessee's execution procedures, particularly after reports emerged that staff struggled to establish intravenous lines before administering the drugs.

Pike's attorneys have also questioned whether warnings about her medical circumstances were adequately considered.

Despite the failed attempt, Pike remains on death row. Lee's latest remarks indicate that the state has not abandoned the sentence imposed for her role in the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer , although the precise legal and practical implications of another execution attempt remain uncertain.

The failed execution has triggered a wider investigation

Pike's execution was halted after the lethal-injection drugs failed to bring about her death.

According to a detailed account submitted by one of her attorneys, officials made repeated attempts to establish intravenous access, using approximately 10 needles and trying several locations on both arms.

The attorney's account described concerns among members of the execution team that some of Pike's veins might have ruptured. Pike reportedly complained that her arm was burning before she began making unusual breathing sounds.

Her legal team subsequently pressed officials to stop the procedure and obtain emergency medical assistance.

Pike was taken to hospital, where she spent days receiving treatment. At one stage, she was unconscious and required a ventilator, with her attorneys fearing she might not survive.

She eventually regained consciousness, recovered sufficiently to speak and walk again, and was discharged back into prison custody.

The incident has had consequences beyond Pike's individual case. Lee ordered a comprehensive, independent investigation and suspended scheduled executions in Tennessee through the end of 2026 while officials examine what went wrong.

Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada also announced his resignation in the aftermath of the failed procedure.

The investigation could prove important in determining whether the execution team followed the state's established protocol and whether changes are necessary before any future executions take place.

Why Christa Pike remains on death row

Pike was sentenced to death for her involvement in the January 1995 killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer , a fellow participant in the Job Corps programme in Knoxville, Tennessee. Court records describe a prolonged and brutal attack involving Pike and two other people.

Pike was convicted of first-degree murder in 1996. She also received a separate conviction for attempted first-degree murder following an assault on another inmate in 2001. She has remained in state custody for more than three decades.

The case attracted renewed attention before the September execution because Pike was scheduled to become the first woman executed by Tennessee in more than 200 years.

Her attorneys had sought clemency, but Lee declined to intervene before the scheduled procedure. The U.S. Supreme Court also denied her application for a stay on September 29.

For now, the governor's latest comments make clear that the failed procedure has not itself resulted in a commutation or cancellation of Pike's sentence.

However, the pause on executions means Tennessee will not carry out another scheduled execution before the end of 2026 under the current suspension.

The immediate focus is now on the findings of the independent review and the ongoing legal proceedings. Those developments could shape the state's future approach to lethal injections, but Pike's ultimate fate remains unresolved.

Lee has signalled that her death sentence remains in force unless the courts determine otherwise. Whether Tennessee will attempt to carry it out again, and when such a decision might be possible, remains an open question.

articles.title: Trump's national security warning: Golf course deemed "deadly danger" to White House staff
articles.standfirst: Donald Trump has demanded the immediate closure of Washington's East Potomac Golf Course after claiming a White House staff member was struck in the chest by a stray golf ball
articles.summary: Donald Trump has demanded the immediate closure of Washington's East Potomac Golf Course after claiming a White House staff member was struck in the chest by a stray golf ball
articles.body:
President Donald Trump has called for an immediate shutdown of a public golf facility in Washington, D.C., after alleging that a White House staffer suffered an injury when a golf ball flew into an area where people were present.

In a Truth Social post on Thursday, October 29, Trump criticised the condition of East Potomac Golf Links, arguing that damaged infrastructure and inadequate protection around its driving range had created an unacceptable safety risk.

“Golf balls soar through the holes at high speed and hit unexpecting Golfers—including a White House staffer who was, sadly, hit violently in the chest. The driving range building itself is falling apart, and its structural stability is terrible. It should be closed immediately for safety reasons! The exposed nails and disintegrating wood also endanger young Golfers — Not a good situation!” the post said.

Trump did not identify the injured staff member or provide further details about the person's condition.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged incident have not been independently established in the available reporting.

The president also argued that Washington residents deserved a safer and better-maintained facility, promising that a redevelopment would improve the experience for local golfers.

“The people of Washington, D.C., (and the Nation!) deserve so much better, like a beautiful, safe, affordable, accessible, sanitary, and CLEAN driving range! No one will be more thrilled by our plans to renovate the Course and Driving Range than the Local Golfers who have played there for years, and have begged to have their Home Course brought into pristine condition. The driving range should provide Golfers with stunning views of the Washington Monument, not of a barren, debris-ridden wasteland. The driving range should NOT be a threat to life and limb.”

A safety complaint becomes part of a wider legal battle

The demand for closure comes amid an ongoing dispute over Trump's plans to transform the historic public course into a championship-level facility.

East Potomac Golf Links has long provided relatively affordable golf in the nation's capital. However, Trump's proposed overhaul has faced opposition from preservation advocates and local golfers concerned about the impact on the park and public access.

The dispute escalated after hundreds of trees were removed from the site earlier this month. U.S. District Judge Ana C. Reyes subsequently issued a preliminary injunction prohibiting further tree removal or damage and requiring advance written notice before certain irreversible changes.

Trump has criticised the judge and indicated that his administration intends to appeal.

Federal officials have also said the course is expected to close on November 15 as the government moves forward with plans for redevelopment, although the project remains subject to legal and procedural requirements.

In his latest post, Trump renewed his criticism of the existing facility and promised a major transformation.

“The current condition of the golf course is a National Disgrace, but we will make it a WORLD CLASS PUBLIC Golf Course that is AFFORDABLE for locals — Just like the Great and Historic Public Courses of Torrey Pines and Bethpage Black, only better, for the good of our now Beautiful Again Washington, D.C. After we are done, the East Potomac Course will be a place of immeasurable Pride for the City, all of the Golf Enthusiasts who live here, a Course worthy of and befitting our Nation’s Capital. We will hold the judge, Ana C. Reyes, fully responsible for anybody who is hurt, or killed, on this very dangerous, dilapidated, and unsightly Golf Course.”

The administration's proposed closure and redesign remain central to the legal dispute, with preservation groups challenging how the project is being carried out. A new design by golf architect Tom Fazio is expected to undergo further review.

Trump's latest safety claims add another dimension to the controversy, but they do not resolve the questions before the court. For now, the identity of the staffer who was allegedly struck, the severity of the injury and the precise circumstances of the incident remain unclear.

The immediate question is whether the planned closure and redevelopment can proceed on the administration's proposed timetable while the court's restrictions remain in force.

articles.title: Donald Trump turns the White House into the setting for Halloween: candy, costumes, and even an Air Force One flight
articles.standfirst: The second time, during Trump’s second term, that the presidential couple has organized this celebration ahead of Halloween night
articles.summary: The second time, during Trump’s second term, that the presidential couple has organized this celebration ahead of Halloween night
articles.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump celebrated the traditional Halloween party at the White House, where they handed out candy to thousands of children in an atmosphere marked by costumes, pumpkins, and autumn decorations.

Fresh from a campaign event in South Carolina, the president joined Melania at one of the entrances to the South Lawn of the presidential residence to take part in the classic "trick-or-treating" . The event, open to officials, military personnel, and invited families, was expected to bring together around 6,000 people.

This is the second time, during Trump's second term, that the presidential couple has hosted this celebration ahead of Halloween night, one of the most popular and eagerly anticipated holidays on the American calendar.

Melania , dressed in a brown trench coat by Noor Hammour and Manolo Blahnik shoes, accompanied the president during the candy distribution. Both posed with children dressed up as all kinds of characters, from wizards and dinosaurs to police officers and historical figures such as George Washington or Abraham Lincoln.

One of the most striking moments of the day came when Trump signed what appeared to be a replica of the Declaration of Independence carried by one of the attendees . Also drawing attention was an enormous pumpkin provided by the Department of Agriculture, which became one of the day’s main attractions for photographs.

This is what the White House looked like

The White House featured decorations dominated by orange and reddish tones, with a large depiction of the so-called "Harvest Moon" as one of the most prominent elements. In addition, attendees were able to enjoy stands with coloring books, science kits, and various toys distributed throughout the residence's gardens.

In addition, the Air Force Strolling Strings band livened up the celebration with traditional Halloween tunes and some classics that even got the president dancing.

The finishing touch came from the sky. A spectacular flyover by Air Force One surprised the guests , who responded with applause as they watched the presidential aircraft pass at close range over the White House.

articles.title: What are the Social Security Proposals that candidates have made for the 2026 Midterm Elections?
articles.standfirst: With Social Security's main trust fund projected to run short in 2032, candidates are facing growing pressure to explain how they would protect benefits
articles.summary: With Social Security's main trust fund projected to run short in 2032, candidates are facing growing pressure to explain how they would protect benefits
articles.body:
The issue has become particularly important in Senate contests because the lawmakers elected in November will still be serving when the funding deadline arrives.

Under current projections, the programme will not be able to pay the full benefits currently promised if Congress fails to act. The Peter G. Peterson Foundation cites a potential immediate reduction of 22% for beneficiaries once the main trust fund is depleted.

Scripps News puts the projected cut at approximately 20%, while other estimates vary depending on the assumptions used.

The financial challenge is partly driven by demographic changes. As the American population ages, more people are claiming retirement benefits while the number of workers paying into the system has not increased at the same pace.

Social Security therefore faces growing pressure to balance incoming contributions with payments to retirees, disabled people and surviving family members.

One of the most prominent proposals is to increase or completely remove the cap on earnings subject to Social Security payroll taxes.

In 2026, the taxable maximum is $184,500, meaning earnings above that threshold are not subject to the programme's standard payroll tax.

Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan supports removing the limit, arguing that higher earners should contribute more.

His Republican opponent, Mike Rogers , has highlighted the importance of tackling fraud when discussing potential improvements to the programme.

The same debate is playing out in Maine, where Democratic candidate Troy Jackson has pledged to eliminate the cap. He told CBS News: "People who work hard their entire lives should be able to retire with dignity," Jackson said in a statement to CBS News.

"While Susan Collins has repeatedly voted to weaken Social Security , I'll work to scrap the cap because billionaires should pay into Social Security at the same rate teachers and loggers do. Social Security is a promise, and I intend to keep it."

Which other candidates have offered plans to protect Social Security?

Republican Senator Susan Collins , who is facing Jackson in Maine, has suggested a different route.

She has called for a bipartisan commission to examine possible solutions to the programme's financial difficulties, including "such as potentially raising the earnings cap for Social Security taxes." Collins has also said she does not support cutting benefits.

Her position illustrates how some Republicans are open to increasing the amount of income subject to payroll taxes, even if they have not endorsed the same approach as their Democratic opponents.

Collins previously worked with Democrat Sherrod Brown on the Social Security Fairness Act, which became law in 2025 and removed rules that had reduced certain public-sector retirees' benefits.

The debate over the taxable maximum extends beyond Michigan and Maine. An analysis published by economist Jon Schwabish on October 27 examined 41 candidates across 20 Senate races. It found that 20 candidates had supported raising or eliminating the cap.

Thirteen of the 17 Democrats included in the research backed such a change, alongside all four independent candidates. Only three of the 20 Republicans had publicly endorsed it.

Among the Republicans who support changing the limit are Collins, Massachusetts candidate John Deaton and Kansas Senator Roger Marshall . Marshall has said he would "eliminate the cap altogether."

In contrast, Ohio Republican Jon Husted has opposed the approach, saying he was "not on board" with eliminating the limit. Democrat Sherrod Brown supports raising it.

Other candidates have discussed asking wealthier Americans to contribute more without committing to a precise change. North Carolina Democrat Roy Cooper and New Hampshire Democrat Chris Pappas have both expressed support for higher contributions from affluent earners, but have not endorsed a specific adjustment to the taxable maximum.

Georgia Democrat Jon Ossoff has focused instead on repealing the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which he argues brought forward the projected funding deadline.

Not every proposal involves raising taxes. Potential alternatives include gradually increasing the retirement age, reducing benefits for higher-income retirees, introducing limits on the maximum payments households can receive, or finding additional revenue through other sources.

These options remain politically contentious because they could shift costs onto particular groups of workers or beneficiaries.

The political pressure to produce a credible plan is clear. A September survey commissioned by the Peterson Foundation found that 81% of voters in five competitive Senate states were more likely to support a candidate with a plan to prevent automatic benefit cuts than one who simply promised not to change Social Security.

Overall, 91% supported reform, while 77% said delaying action made the problem harder to solve.

Despite the range of ideas, there is no single agreed solution across the candidates. Some want higher earners to pay more, others favour commissions or tackling fraud, while many have promised to protect benefits without explaining exactly how they would finance them.

The November elections will determine who has a role in shaping the next stage of the debate, but preventing the projected cuts will ultimately require congressional action.

Scripps News puts the projected cut at approximately 20%, while other estimates vary depending on the assumptions used.

The financial challenge is partly driven by demographic changes. As the American population ages, more people are claiming retirement benefits while the number of workers paying into the system has not increased at the same pace.
Social Security therefore faces growing pressure to balance incoming contributions with payments to retirees, disabled people and surviving family members.
One of the most prominent proposals is to increase or completely remove the cap on earnings subject to Social Security payroll taxes.
In 2026, the taxable maximum is $184,500, meaning earnings above that threshold are not subject to the programme's standard payroll tax.
Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan supports removing the limit, arguing that higher earners should contribute more.
His Republican opponent, Mike Rogers , has highlighted the importance of tackling fraud when discussing potential improvements to the programme.

The same debate is playing out in Maine, where Democratic candidate Troy Jackson has pledged to eliminate the cap. He told CBS News: "People who work hard their entire lives should be able to retire with dignity," Jackson said in a statement to CBS News.

"While Susan Collins has repeatedly voted to weaken Social Security , I'll work to scrap the cap because billionaires should pay into Social Security at the same rate teachers and loggers do. Social Security is a promise, and I intend to keep it."
Which other candidates have offered plans to protect Social Security?
Republican Senator Susan Collins , who is facing Jackson in Maine, has suggested a different route.

She has called for a bipartisan commission to examine possible solutions to the programme's financial difficulties, including "such as potentially raising the earnings cap for Social Security taxes." Collins has also said she does not support cutting benefits.
Her position illustrates how some Republicans are open to increasing the amount of income subject to payroll taxes, even if they have not endorsed the same approach as their Democratic opponents.
Collins previously worked with Democrat Sherrod Brown on the Social Security Fairness Act, which became law in 2025 and removed rules that had reduced certain public-sector retirees' benefits.

The debate over the taxable maximum extends beyond Michigan and Maine. An analysis published by economist Jon Schwabish on October 27 examined 41 candidates across 20 Senate races. It found that 20 candidates had supported raising or eliminating the cap.
Thirteen of the 17 Democrats included in the research backed such a change, alongside all four independent candidates. Only three of the 20 Republicans had publicly endorsed it.
Among the Republicans who support changing the limit are Collins, Massachusetts candidate John Deaton and Kansas Senator Roger Marshall . Marshall has said he would "eliminate the cap altogether."
In contrast, Ohio Republican Jon Husted has opposed the approach, saying he was "not on board" with eliminating the limit. Democrat Sherrod Brown supports raising it.

Other candidates have discussed asking wealthier Americans to contribute more without committing to a precise change. North Carolina Democrat Roy Cooper and New Hampshire Democrat Chris Pappas have both expressed support for higher contributions from affluent earners, but have not endorsed a specific adjustment to the taxable maximum.
Georgia Democrat Jon Ossoff has focused instead on repealing the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which he argues brought forward the projected funding deadline.

Not every proposal involves raising taxes. Potential alternatives include gradually increasing the retirement age, reducing benefits for higher-income retirees, introducing limits on the maximum payments households can receive, or finding additional revenue through other sources.
These options remain politically contentious because they could shift costs onto particular groups of workers or beneficiaries.

The political pressure to produce a credible plan is clear. A September survey commissioned by the Peterson Foundation found that 81% of voters in five competitive Senate states were more likely to support a candidate with a plan to prevent automatic benefit cuts than one who simply promised not to change Social Security.
Overall, 91% supported reform, while 77% said delaying action made the problem harder to solve.

Despite the range of ideas, there is no single agreed solution across the candidates. Some want higher earners to pay more, others favour commissions or tackling fraud, while many have promised to protect benefits without explaining exactly how they would finance them.
The November elections will determine who has a role in shaping the next stage of the debate, but preventing the projected cuts will ultimately require congressional action.

articles.title: Epstein was killed in a "violent struggle in his cell": Explosive investigation seeks to overturn official suicide ruling
articles.standfirst: An independent team of forensic specialists is preparing to present new findings about Jeffrey Epstein’s death, raising fresh questions about injuries found on his body and the handling of evidence at the New York prison
articles.summary: An independent team of forensic specialists is preparing to present new findings about Jeffrey Epstein’s death, raising fresh questions about injuries found on his body and the handling of evidence at the New York prison
articles.body:
J effrey Epstein ’s death inside a Manhattan jail in August 2019 is once again under scrutiny, with an international team of forensic specialists preparing to challenge the official conclusion that the disgraced financier died by suicide.

Dr. Michael Freeman , a forensic medicine professor affiliated with the Royal College of Pathologists in London, is leading the review.

Following approximately a year of work, he is expected to present the findings to fellow specialists on November 16, potentially adding another chapter to one of the most controversial deaths in recent American criminal history.

According to the investigation reported by RadarOnline.com, Freeman’s team has examined medical records, photographs and hundreds of pages of material provided by Epstein’s brother, Mark.

The review has reportedly identified injuries that the researchers believe deserve further examination, including marks around the face, neck and shoulder, as well as scratches near the ligature marks.

Freeman believes some of these details could be significant when assessing whether Epstein struggled before his death. The official determination, however, remains suicide by hanging, and the new investigation has not established that a homicide occurred.

While the Department of Justice (DOJ) said: "Jeffrey Epstein died by suicide," Freeman asserted Epstein "was trying to get at the ligature that was around his neck, which would not have occurred in the circumstances of a hanging."

Freeman has also raised concerns about the transparency of the original investigation. He declined to disclose the full conclusions ahead of his November presentation, telling RadarOnline.com: "What I hope to show is that we need to have a little bit more transparency about how the investigation was done, because this whole thing has been very occult."

Questions surrounding the autopsy and missing evidence

The renewed examination also revisits concerns previously raised by Dr. Michael Baden , the independent pathologist appointed by Epstein’s brother to observe the 2019 autopsy.

Baden questioned whether fractures discovered in Epstein’s neck were consistent with suicide, arguing that they could indicate homicidal strangulation.

New York City’s Chief Medical Examiner, Dr. Barbara Sampson , rejected that interpretation and maintained that the injuries supported her office’s conclusion.

Baden’s concerns have remained part of the debate, although they have never resulted in an official change to the cause or manner of death.

Freeman has separately questioned why the ligature allegedly used in the hanging was not preserved for further examination. "They did not preserve the ligature," Freeman said.

The FBI disputed criticism of its handling of the case, stating: "This is completely false. FBI agents followed all appropriate procedures."

There are also serious questions about the prison’s security arrangements. Epstein was found dead at the Metropolitan Correctional Center on August 10, 2019, while awaiting trial on federal sex-trafficking charges.

Staff were supposed to conduct regular checks, but the Justice Department’s inspector general later established that required rounds and inmate counts were not completed during the night. Records were also falsified, and a malfunctioning recording system left investigators with limited surveillance footage.

The 2023 inspector general report nevertheless found no evidence contradicting the FBI’s conclusion that there was no criminality connected to Epstein’s death.

Investigators said the available footage showed nobody entering his cell tier during the relevant overnight period. The report also noted that the medical examiner found no defensive injuries expected in a fatal struggle.

A separate FBI review released by the Justice Department in 2025 again concluded that Epstein died by suicide, citing the autopsy and surveillance footage.

Freeman’s team includes Swedish forensic pathology expert Dr. Anders Eriksson and British specialist Dr. Itiel Dror, who studies bias and errors in forensic science. The group’s findings are expected to receive considerable attention when presented in November.

Mark Epstein has expressed support for the work, telling RadarOnline.com that "the truth will eventually come out," while describing the findings as "compelling and convincing."

Freeman also questioned why so little information was available about the circumstances surrounding the death of such a high-profile prisoner.

"We have one of the most notorious prisoners in a jail, a person of great public interest who dies under what is reasonably called suspicious circumstances, and we have virtually no information on what those circumstances are," said Freeman , pointing out only one person reportedly saw Jeffrey hanging.

"What makes this a very, very unusual suicide by hanging determination. In fact, I've never seen anything like this before."

The November presentation could renew pressure for greater disclosure and further scrutiny of the original investigation.

However, until the findings are made public and independently assessed, the official ruling remains unchanged: Epstein’s death was classified as suicide.

articles.title: From the Vatican to Illinois: Pope Leo XIV Becomes First Pontiff to Vote in a U.S. Election
articles.standfirst: He has participated in U.S. elections whenever he has been able to
articles.summary: He has participated in U.S. elections whenever he has been able to
articles.body:
P ope Leo XIV has already exercised his right to vote ahead of the midterm legislative elections that the United States will hold next November 3 . The Pontiff has sent his ballot by mail to Chicago , as confirmed this Friday by the Vatican press office.

The Holy See explained that Leo XIV has participated in U.S. electoral processes whenever possible as a citizen of the country, maintaining a practice that he has now repeated from the Vatican by voting by mail.

In a statement, the Vatican also emphasized that the Pope considers participation at the ballot box to be part of the rights and responsibilities of any citizen within a democratic system.

With this gesture, Leo XIV once again demonstrates his commitment to civic participation , exercising a right he retains as a U.S. citizen despite currently holding the highest office in the Catholic Church.

Pope Leo XIV and his point of tension with Trump in the past

The relationship between the President of the United States, Donald Trump, and Pope Leo XIV (the first pontiff of American origin) escalated into an unprecedented diplomatic conflict between Washington and the Holy See . The confrontation combined deep ethical and geopolitical differences, as well as personal disputes on social media.

articles.title: An American football coach and a Disney World employee are among nearly 300 people arrested for sexual harassment
articles.standfirst: Florida authorities uncover alleged child predators and human trafficking networks in a major weeklong operation
articles.summary: Florida authorities uncover alleged child predators and human trafficking networks in a major weeklong operation
articles.body:
A major undercover operation in Florida has resulted in 281 arrests, including a youth football coach, a former Walt Disney World character performer and several theme park employees.

The weeklong investigation, named Operation Polk Around and Find Out II, was led by the Polk County Sheriff's Office with support from multiple law enforcement agencies.

Authorities said the operation involved two separate investigations. One targeted adults allegedly attempting to arrange sexual encounters with minors, while the other focused on prostitution and suspected human trafficking networks.

Collectively, those arrested face 488 new criminal charges, including 198 felonies and 290 misdemeanours.

Among the cases highlighted by Sheriff Grady Judd was that of 24-year-old Colin Klaco , who reportedly told investigators he had previously worked as a Mickey Mouse performer at Disney World.

According to Judd, Klaco arrived carrying two backpacks filled with diapers, which he allegedly intended to use during an encounter with someone he believed was a young boy. The individual was actually an undercover investigator.

Another Disney employee, Adam Snyder , worked at the Roundup Rodeo restaurant in Toy Story Land. Police said he was arrested while allegedly still wearing his work uniform after attempting to arrange a sexual encounter with someone he believed was a minor.

Also among those arrested was 31-year-old Rashion Crayton , a local youth football coach whose online conversations with an undercover officer posing as a 14-year-old girl reportedly contained explicit messages.

Undercover operation exposes alleged predators and trafficking victims

Judd described Crayton's communications as particularly disturbing, claiming the coach had discussed collecting the supposed teenager from school before engaging in sexual activity.

An active-duty US Navy sailor, 24-year-old Dang Thai , was also arrested after allegedly communicating with someone he believed was underage. Officials said he claimed to be 17 during the online exchange, despite being 24.

The investigation resulted in 31 arrests connected to alleged child sexual predation. A further 239 arrests related to prostitution offences, while 11 others involved separate matters.

Among those accused in the prostitution investigation, 117 allegedly travelled to arrange paid sexual encounters, while 122 were arrested for offering prostitution services. An Orange County deputy was also among those accused of soliciting.

Authorities confirmed that 17 theme park employees were arrested, including 13 connected to Disney and four employed by Universal. Disney confirmed that the employees involved had been dismissed, while Universal also said it had terminated the employment of its arrested workers.

Beyond the arrests, investigators identified 11 individuals believed to be victims of human trafficking. They were offered support and assistance following assessments involving specialist organisations.

Officials said those arrested came from across Florida, 20 other US states and 18 foreign countries, with just 40 suspects living in Polk County.

Florida's attorney general said prosecutors intended to pursue the cases, while Judd urged parents to monitor children's online activities and remain aware of the adults involved in their lives.

articles.title: Christa Pike breaks her silence after her execution fails: “The pain is not just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul"
articles.standfirst: Christa Pike describes constant pain in first statement since her failed execution
articles.summary: Christa Pike describes constant pain in first statement since her failed execution
articles.body:
C hrista Pike said Friday she remains in constant pain, struggles to speak and has been largely isolated in a prison hospital after surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee last month.

In her first public statement since, Pike said she's “deeply hurt by the incompetence that has put so many people in this terrible position.”

“I continue to think about my victim’s family, ” she said, “and the terrible pain and loss they have endured.”

PPike and her boyfriend tortured and stabbed a 19-year-old classmate, Colleen Slemmer , to death in 1995. Pike was 18 at the time, making her one of the youngest women sentenced to death. Slemmer’s mother traveled from Florida to witness Pike’s execution.

Pike, 50, survived two doses of pentobarbital that her lawyers say probably didn't enter her bloodstream correctly and instead pooled in her arms, leaving them burned and blistered. Unconscious, she was hospitalized on a ventilator for days, and at one point her lawyers said they didn't expect her to survive.

“There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak ,” Pike said. “And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul.”

Pike said she had been prepared to die in peace, but instead woke up alone and confused in a hospital bed. She said she's “searching for meaning in what happened to me.”

“I don’t know why I survived that night. I don’t know what comes next,” Pike said in a statement dictated to her legal team from prison.

“I continue to think about my victim’s family

Pike remains sentenced to die, and her attorneys want Republican Gov. Bill Lee to change that to life in prison. However, Lee told reporters this week, “I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless determined otherwise by the courts .”

The governor has tapped a former U.S. attorney to conduct an independent review of the failed execution, and postponed the state’s other lethal injection scheduled for this year.

Pike's attorneys, meanwhile, asked a federal judge Friday to allow her to interact with other prisoners instead of being isolated in the infirmary. They said her isolation violates a 2024 agreement that ended her mostly solitary confinement and allowed her to work, eat, exercise and have social contact with other women.

“Her renewed isolation has caused, and will continue to cause, significant psychological harm and trauma,” Pike's legal team wrote.

Pike's lethal injection was plagued by problems. Her attorneys had warned that her small veins and diagnosis of thrombocytosis, a blood-clotting disorder, could make IV access difficult.

In a court document, her attorney Randy Spivey said the execution team struggled to get working IV lines in Pike’s arms and expressed concern that a vein might be “blowing.” Pike remained awake for much of the lethal injection, saying her arm hurt and burned before falling unconscious. The execution began just before 7:30 p.m. and an ambulance arrived at the prison about an hour and 45 minutes later.

The failed execution has brought renewed scrutiny to how Tennessee carries out death sentences.

In a 2025 deposition released with court documents this week, prison Warden Kenneth Nelson said the execution team doesn't practice inserting IV lines during training sessions, at the directive of the prison commissioner. Nelson said he did not know why the practice was discontinued or when the order was given.

Practicing insertion of IVs was part of Tennessee’s prior execution protocol, but it is not included in the state’s new protocol.

Dorinda Carter, a spokesperson for the Tennessee Department of Correction, said she could not comment on the filing because of pending litigation.

Frank Strada , commissioner of the Department of Correction, announced his resignation in the wake of Pike's failed execution. The governor named Christopher Hansen as interim commissioner.

articles.title: When is the Alaska Permanent Fund payment made in November 2026 and who is getting it this month?
articles.standfirst: Alaska Permanent Fund payment date is Thursday, November 19
articles.summary: Alaska Permanent Fund payment date is Thursday, November 19
articles.body:
Alaska residents waiting for their Permanent Fund Dividend (PFD) have another payment date to look forward to in November as the next distribution is scheduled for November 19, with eligible applicants whose claims have reached the required processing status set to receive their money.

The payment applies to 2026 and prior-year dividend applications that are listed as “Eligible-Not Paid” on November 11 and applicants who meet that status requirement are included in the November 19 distribution.

Although the payment is not being sent automatically to every resident, the Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend is an annual payment that gives qualifying residents a share of the financial benefits generated by the state's natural resources.

Residents must also have satisfied the eligibility conditions applicable to the dividend year for which they applied otherwise they may not receive the payment as applicants generally needed to maintain Alaska residency throughout 2025.

Residents must also intend to remain in the state indefinitely and meet the physical-presence requirements and those rules include spending at least 72 consecutive hours physically in Alaska during 2024 or 2025.

Applicants who were outside the state for more than 180 days during 2025 must also demonstrate that their absence qualified under an approved legal category.

Who is receiving the November 2026 payment?

Unlike many government assistance programmes, the Alaskan PFD is not determined by an applicant's income, employment status or financial circumstances and the November distribution is intended for people with a current or previous-year application marked “Eligible-Not Paid” on November 11.

Applicants who have not yet reached the required stage of approval may not be included in this particular payment round but there is no cause for concern just yet as November 19 is one of two remaining distribution dates listed for 2026 and previous-year applications.

The schedule also included an October payment and another distribution in December for applicants who reach the required status by the relevant cutoff. Applications marked “Eligible-Not Paid” were paid on October 12 whilst the next dates due up are on November 19 and December 17.

The dates mean that an applicant's processing status on the specified cutoff day determines which distribution they may enter and someone whose application is not marked “Eligible-Not Paid” by November 11 should not assume they will receive money on November 19.

The investment fund itself was established in 1976 to preserve part of Alaska 's oil wealth for future generations, while the dividend programme began in 1980 and unlike many government assistance schemes, the PFD is not determined by an applicant's income, employment status or financial circumstances.

Recipients can check the progress of their Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend (PFD) application through the official myPFD portal , operated by the Alaska Department of Revenue's Permanent Fund Dividend Division .

Applicants can visit the myPFD portal and log in using the myAlaska account associated with their application and they can also use the application search facility and provide the identifying information requested.

Applicants needing assistance can contact the Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend Division at 907-465-2326 or email dor.pfd.info@alaska.gov .

The investment fund itself was established in 1976 to preserve part of Alaska 's oil wealth for future generations, while the dividend programme began in 1980 and unlike many government assistance schemes, the PFD is not determined by an applicant's income, employment status or financial circumstances.

Recipients can check the progress of their Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend (PFD) application through the official myPFD portal , operated by the Alaska Department of Revenue's Permanent Fund Dividend Division .

Applicants can visit the myPFD portal and log in using the myAlaska account associated with their application and they can also use the application search facility and provide the identifying information requested.
Applicants needing assistance can contact the Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend Division at 907-465-2326 or email dor.pfd.info@alaska.gov .

articles.title: Is Daylight Savings Time ending? This is what President Trump said about a possible change
articles.standfirst: The clocks are due to roll back one hour on Sunday, November 1
articles.summary: The clocks are due to roll back one hour on Sunday, November 1
articles.body:
Daylight Saving Time ends across most of the United States at 2am on Sunday, November 1, when clocks move back one hour to 1am as the change gives people an extra hour of sleep but brings earlier sunsets and more daylight in the morning. However, President Donald Trump wants Congress to end the twice-yearly clock changes, arguing that Americans should no longer have to adjust their clocks and he has repeatedly supported making Daylight Saving Time permanent.

Lawmakers have yet to agree on a way forward, Trump renewed his criticism of the system during a rally in Mississippi on October 26 ahead of the midterms, describing the clock changes as something that "drive everyone crazy." The 80-year-old added that "nobody wants to do (it) anymore," arguing that Americans overwhelmingly oppose changing their clocks as the POTUS acknowledged that people disagree about whether they prefer more daylight in the morning or evening. However, he claimed there was universal support for ending the twice-yearly adjustments, calling the practice costly and dangerous and later Trump accused the Senate of allowing legislation to expire despite widespread public support. "The United States Senate is letting the Daylight Saving Bill die, when a vast Majority of the Country want it," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Most people are demanding light in the evening, but ALL want not to change their clocks anymore." Trump finished the post by demanding lawmakers "TAKE A VOTE!"

Why has the Sunshine Protection Act stalled?

The legislation at the center of the debate is the Sunshine Protection Act as the bill passed the House of Representatives in July 2026 by a vote of 301-117, but has not secured enough support to advance through the Senate . The modern American system developed through several legislative changes. Germany introduced daylight-saving measures in 1916, while the United States followed with the Standard Time Act of 1918 . Congress repealed that arrangement in 1919, although seasonal clock changes returned during wartime. The federal government introduced year-round War Time between 1942 and 1945. The Uniform Time Act of 1966 later established the framework governing the country's time zones and seasonal clock changes, placing the authority to change the system with Congress . An energy crisis prompted another experiment in 1974, when the United States temporarily adopted year-round Daylight Saving Time before further adjustments followed in 1986. Finally, the Energy Policy Act of 2005 extended the annual period beginning in 2007. Supporters argue that longer evenings create more opportunities for outdoor recreation, tourism and commercial activity but critics argue changing clocks can disrupt sleep patterns and the body's internal clock, with potential consequences for health and safety.

articles.title: Midterm Elections 2026 Senate Predictions: Which candidates are more likely to win next Tuesday?
articles.standfirst: Kansas, Texas, Maine and Ohio serve as key battle grounds
articles.summary: Kansas, Texas, Maine and Ohio serve as key battle grounds
articles.body:
Control of the US Senate is at stake when voters go to the polls November 3 with the Republicans defending a 53-47 majority, whilst the Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control. The campaign is shaped by inflation, and household costs remain concerns, while the Iran war has raised questions about its duration, financial impact and fuel prices whilst immigration enforcement is another issue.

President Donald Trump' s approval is part of the political backdrop as Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin average put him at 37%, while the national congressional ballot average showed Democrats ahead by 8.9 points. And the latest surveys point to several close contests as several Republican -held seats are under pressure in states that backed Trump in 2024 – notably in Kansas , Texas , Maine and Ohio . Those battle grounds have produced polling showing Democratic candidates competitive or ahead, creating a challenge for Republicans seeking to preserve their majority and an unlikely turnaround compared to previous voting trends. Kansas has become one of the election's most striking contests as Adam Hamilton leads the Republican Senator Roger Marshall by 54%-44% in a Washington Post survey despite Trump 's 16-point state victory in 2024. Texas is drawing national attention, although its polling is less consistent as James Talarico leads the Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton 49%-43% in a CNN survey and 49%-47% in a Texas Southern University/YouGov poll. In Maine , Democrat Troy Jackson leads Republican Senator Susan Collins 49%-45% in CNN polling as Ohio offers another possible pickup, with former Senator Sherrod Brown ahead of Republican Jon Husted by three points. But the Democrats are also defending seats while seeking gains as in Michigan , Abdul El-Sayed leads Republican Mike Rogers 49%-42% whilst New Hampshire ’s Democrat Chris Pappas leads former Senator John Sununu 48%-41%. Over in North Carolina , former Democratic Governor Roy Cooper leads Republican Michael Whatley 52%-39% and Georgia 's Senator Jon Ossoff is also ahead of Republican Representative Mike Collins , 48%-40%.

What would the Senate result mean for Trump's presidency?

If Democrats win four seats and take the Senate , they would gain control of committees and the power to shape the chamber's agenda as the change would also affect confirmation of cabinet officials, ambassadors and federal judges. A Democratic majority could scrutinize administration decisions through hearings and investigations, whilst making it harder for Trump to secure approval for nominees. Republicans would lose control of the Senate calendar. Although the president would retain his veto and ability to issue execute orders, if Republicans hold their majority, Trump would keep a more supportive Senate for judicial and administration appointments. Retaining both chambers would also give his party greater control over hearings, legislation and the congressional response to the White House , avoiding him becoming a lame duck President in the final years of his tenure. But even a Democratic Senate would not give the party unrestricted power. Major legislation can face the filibuster, and overriding a presidential veto requires a two-thirds majority in both chambers.

articles.summary: One winning ticket managed to take home $100,000 in Pennsylvania
articles.body:
P owerball players across the United States are chasing an estimated $760 million jackpot in Saturday's October 31 drawing as the prize has climbed after nobody matched all six numbers on Wednesday.

The next drawing scheduled for 22:59 ET/19:59 PT with the winning numbers for Saturday not yet been announced, although the jackpot carries an estimated cash value of $326 million.

A potential jackpot winner the choice between a reduced one-time payment and 30 annual installments after Wednesday's October 28 drawing produced the numbers 11, 13, 16, 47 and 60, with 13 as the red Powerball .

The Power Play multiplier was 2X, but no ticket matched all six numbers to claim the jackpot meaning the prize rolls over, although one Pennsylvania ticket did secure a $100,000 prize.

The ticket matched four of the five white balls and the red Powerball , with the Power Play option doubling the standard $50,000 payout and the Pennsylvania Lottery has not disclosed where that winning ticket was purchased.
