articles.title: Who is getting their Social Security check for November this week? Every beneficiary who will get their payment in the coming days
articles.standfirst: Payments are due as soon as Tuesday, November 3
articles.summary: Payments are due as soon as Tuesday, November 3
articles.body:
Millions of Americans are preparing to receive their November Social Security payments, with the first group scheduled to be paid on Tuesday, November 3 as the payment calendar depends on when recipients began claiming benefits. The Social Security Administration distributes retirement, disability and survivor benefits on different dates throughout the month, with most beneficiaries who filed after May 1, 1997, are assigned a Wednesday payment based on their date of birth.

However, people who started receiving benefits before May 1997 follow a separate schedule - and those recipients are due their November payment on Tuesday, November 3, making them the first group to receive money this month. Beneficiaries who began collecting Social Security before May 1997 will receive their payments on November 3 as this group does not follow the birthday-based Wednesday schedule used for most other retirement, disability and survivor recipients. Those who started receiving benefits after May 1, 1997, are divided into three groups according to their birthdays. Anyone born between the first and 10th of a month is scheduled to receive their November payment on Tuesday, November 10. That date differs from the usual second-Wednesday arrangement because November 11 is Veterans Day , a federal holiday so the S ocial Security Administration has moved the payment forward by one day for this group of beneficiaries. Recipients with birthdays between the 11th and 20th of any month will receive their money on Wednesday, November 18. Those born between the 21st and 31st are scheduled for Wednesday, November 25, completing the month's regular payment calendar. Supplemental Security Income recipients follow a different timetable from people receiving retirement, disability or survivor benefits whilst SSI payments normally arrive on the first day of each month, but the November payment is being issued early because November 1 falls on a Sunday. As a result, people receiving SSI can expect their November payment on Friday, October 30, this means the money arrives before November begins, rather than on the first weekday of the new month.

What should you do if your Social Security payment is missing?

Anyone who does not see an expected electronic payment should contact their bank or financial institution first. The Social Security Administration warns that financial institutions can sometimes experience delays when posting payments to accounts. If the money still has not arrived, recipients can report a late, missing or stolen payment by contacting the SSA . The agency can be reached at 1-800-772-1213 , while TTY users can call 1-800-325-0778 . Additionally, recipients who have not reached full retirement age can work while collecting Social Security , but the earnings test may affect their payments. In 2026, those who will not reach FRA during the year can earn up to $24,480 before benefits are withheld. Above that threshold, the SSA withholds $1 in benefits for every $2 earned. The money is not permanently lost, however, as the agency adjusts monthly payments after recipients reach full retirement age. Only income from employment counts toward this earnings limit, meaning dividends and withdrawals from savings and other passive investment income do not reduce Social Security payments under the earnings test.

articles.title: When does Daylight Savings starts in 2027? Date for the next change
articles.standfirst: The clocks went back on Sunday, November 1 but when will they go forwards again?
articles.summary: The clocks went back on Sunday, November 1 but when will they go forwards again?
articles.body:
The next change to daylight saving time in the United States will take place on Sunday, March 14, 2027, when clocks move forward by one hour as the adjustment marks the beginning of longer evening daylight, although it also means darker mornings for people returning to their usual schedules. Most Americans will need to change their clocks at 2:00am local time, moving them directly to 3:00am. The lost hour means that Sunday will be shorter than usual, but daylight saving time will then remain in effect until the autumn.

The United States follows a nationwide timetable established under federal law, with the annual switch taking place on the second Sunday in March and the first Sunday in November. Not every part of the United States observes the clock changes. Hawaii and most of Arizona remain on standard time throughout the year, although the Navajo Nation in Arizona does observe daylight saving time. American Samoa , Guam , the Northern Mariana Islands , Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands also do not participate.

When does daylight saving time end in 2027?

The autumn change is scheduled for Sunday, November 7, 2027. At 2:00am, clocks will move back one hour to 1:00am, returning most of the country to standard time and giving people an additional hour during the night. The 2027 dates differ from those in 2026, when daylight saving time began on March 8 and ended on November 1 as the calendar determines the precise Sundays each year, but the underlying federal schedule remains unchanged. The current system is rooted in the Uniform Time Act of 1966, signed by President Lyndon Johnson . It established consistent rules for states choosing to observe daylight saving time, replacing a confusing arrangement in which cities and states could follow different schedules. The practice itself dates back earlier in American history. The country first introduced daylight saving time in 1918 during World War I , partly as an effort to conserve fuel. It was abolished after the conflict, before returning nationally during World War II under President Franklin Roosevelt 's year-round wartime clock system. Today's March and November schedule was introduced in 2007 following the Energy Policy Act of 2005 , which extended the period of daylight saving time but there have also been renewed efforts to make the arrangement permanent. The Senate passed the Sunshine Protection Act in 2022, but it did not become law and whilst a reintroduced version passed the House in 2026, although Senate approval remains outstanding. Until federal legislation changes the system, Americans should expect the clocks to move forward on March 14 and back on November 7 in 2027.

articles.title: What happens if a President loses the Midterm Election? Every possible consequence of a Democrats win
articles.standfirst: Voters head to the polls on Tuesday, November 3 and the ramifications could determine the course of the United States government
articles.summary: Voters head to the polls on Tuesday, November 3 and the ramifications could determine the course of the United States government
articles.body:
ADemocrat victory in the 2026 Midterm Elections would not remove Donald Trump from the presidency, but it could substantially change the political balance in Washington as control of either chamber of Congress would give Democrats new powers to investigate his administration. Americans vote on November 3, with all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats contested, with Republicans currently controlling both chambers. Democrats could take the House , the Senate or both, and each outcome would impose different limits on Trump 's agenda.

The Democrats would be capable of challenging the priorities of the Trump Administration and obstructing parts of his legislative agenda, but the consequences would ultimately depend heavily on the success of the Democrats . A divided Congress would create different constraints from a Democratic takeover of both chambers, while presidential veto powers and existing constitutional rules would remain in place. Control of Congress would determine how easily he can pass laws, approve spending and secure appointments as midterms determine which party controls each chamber for the next two years. If Democrats win either, Trump would face a Congress less willing to approve his proposals, while committee leadership and oversight powers would shift away from Republicans .

What could happen if Democrats take control of Congress?

A Democratic House could investigate administration decisions, federal spending and possible conflicts of interest as committees could hold hearings, demand records and issue subpoenas, examining whether presidential power benefited Trump , his allies or donors. Potential inquiries could include corporate donors, alleged pay-to-play arrangements and foreign sovereign wealth investments in Trump -linked businesses, and these are possible subjects for scrutiny, not proof of wrongdoing; officials could challenge congressional demands. Democrats could pursue impeachment, too as the House can approve articles by a simple majority, but impeachment does not remove a President - only a conviction at a Senate trial, which requires a two-thirds vote, makes removal a separate and much higher hurdle. Even without removal, hearings and investigations could dominate Washington , expose internal communications and consume administration time whilst a further impeachment vote could deepen political divisions and shape debate ahead of the 2028 Presidential Election .

Could Trump refuse to accept the results of the midterm elections?

Winning the Senate would give Democrats control of its committees and power to block or delay Trump 's cabinet, agency and judicial nominees and that could extend to a Supreme Court vacancy if one arose before his term ends. If Democrats win only the House then Senate Republicans could block most Democratic bills whilst control of both chambers would let Democrats pass proposals on healthcare, abortion rights, tariffs and living costs. Trump could veto legislation he opposes and still has executive orders in his pocket but overriding a veto requires two-thirds support in both chambers, while most Senate bills need 60 votes to overcome a filibuster. Even unified Democratic control would leave major legislative changes difficult without bipartisan support as budget and debt-ceiling negotiations could become flashpoints, bringing spending standoffs or shutdown threats. Trump would still retain broad authority over trade, immigration and foreign policy, and could pursue executive actions within the law as Reuters reports The White House is preparing unilateral options on tariffs, immigration, housing and spending if Democrats win. Courts could block actions exceeding presidential authority, while Congress could investigate implementation or seek to restrict funding and concerns also surround possible challenges to election results or use of the Insurrection Act . The law permits domestic troop deployments only in specified exceptional circumstances; it is not a general power to suppress opposition or control elections, and Trump has threatened to invoke the Insurrection Act “if necessary” in Democrat cities.

If Democrats win only the House then Senate Republicans could block most Democratic bills whilst control of both chambers would let Democrats pass proposals on healthcare, abortion rights, tariffs and living costs. Trump could veto legislation he opposes and still has executive orders in his pocket but overriding a veto requires two-thirds support in both chambers, while most Senate bills need 60 votes to overcome a filibuster. Even unified Democratic control would leave major legislative changes difficult without bipartisan support as budget and debt-ceiling negotiations could become flashpoints, bringing spending standoffs or shutdown threats. Trump would still retain broad authority over trade, immigration and foreign policy, and could pursue executive actions within the law as Reuters reports The White House is preparing unilateral options on tariffs, immigration, housing and spending if Democrats win. Courts could block actions exceeding presidential authority, while Congress could investigate implementation or seek to restrict funding and concerns also surround possible challenges to election results or use of the Insurrection Act . The law permits domestic troop deployments only in specified exceptional circumstances; it is not a general power to suppress opposition or control elections, and Trump has threatened to invoke the Insurrection Act “if necessary” in Democrat cities.

articles.title: Private jet carrying nine crashes near President Trump's Mar-a-Lago in devastating Florida explosion
articles.standfirst: A Learjet 60 crashed into a residential neighborhood in Palm Beach County, just miles from the president's estate
articles.summary: A Learjet 60 crashed into a residential neighborhood in Palm Beach County, just miles from the president's estate
articles.body:
A private jet carrying nine people plunged into a residential area near Palm Beach , Florida, on Sunday afternoon, causing a devastating explosion and leaving emergency crews searching through burning wreckage just miles from President Donald Trump 's Mar-a-Lago estate.

The Learjet 60 crashed at approximately 12:50pm local time near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North in Greenacres, striking an area close to homes and businesses before erupting into flames.

Witnesses described an enormous explosion that shook nearby buildings, while footage captured the aircraft descending rapidly before a fireball engulfed the crash site.

The impact scattered debris across the surrounding area, damaged power lines and left a substantial crater as thick black smoke rose above the neighborhood.

Reports indicated that several people had died, with one subsequent account placing the death toll at nine. However, the number of fatalities hasn't been consistently confirmed.

The crash occurred approximately eight miles from Mar-a-Lago , where President Trump had hosted a Halloween celebration the previous evening before reportedly departing Florida for a campaign appearance in Iowa.

The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed that the twin-engine aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was travelling toward North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas.

"A Learjet 60 crashed in a residential area near Cresthaven, Florida, around 12.50 pm local time on Sunday, November 1. Nine people were on board," the agency said.

Flight-tracking information indicated that the aircraft experienced a sudden descent shortly before impact, although investigators have not established what caused it to lose altitude.

Initial reports suggested the jet struck trees and brought down electrical infrastructure before crashing near a mobile home park.

The FAA confirmed that the National Transportation Safety Board would lead the investigation, examining flight data, physical evidence and other information to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident.

Emergency services respond to disaster

Palm Beach County emergency personnel descended on the scene as firefighters attempted to contain the flames and assess damage to surrounding properties.

The sheriff's office closed Military Trail in both directions between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North, urging motorists to avoid the area while rescue operations continued.

Nearby residents described hearing an exceptionally loud impact, with some comparing the explosion to a missile strike. Others reported temporary power outages following the crash.

Emergency responders initially treated the incident as a mass casualty event, while authorities worked to establish whether anyone on the ground had been injured.

Although the aircraft came down within several miles of Trump's Florida residence, officials have not reported any connection between the flight and the president.

Investigators now face the task of determining why the jet suddenly descended over a populated area, while authorities continue assessing the full human and structural consequences of Sunday's disaster.

articles.title: Donald Trump is already on RSF's list of press predators: for his attacks and restrictions
articles.standfirst: Alongside names such as the president of Russia, Vladimir Putin; that of Nicaragua, Daniel Ortega; or that of Belarus, Alexander Lukashenko
articles.summary: Alongside names such as the president of Russia, Vladimir Putin; that of Nicaragua, Daniel Ortega; or that of Belarus, Alexander Lukashenko
articles.body:
The constant attacks launched by the President of the United States, Donald Trump, are beginning to have consequences . One of them concerns the press . For this reason, the top U.S. leader has been added to the list of press predators compiled by Reporters Without Borders (RSF) , due to his ongoing attacks aimed at reducing journalism to political communication and the restrictions he has imposed on information professionals.

This report that names names came to light this Monday, and Trump is not the only one listed among those singled out. Other leaders had already appeared in previous editions and have continued using the apparatus of the State to muzzle the media, such as the presidents of Russia, Vladimir Putin; Nicaragua, Daniel Ortega; and Belarus, Alexander Lukashenko .

Reasons for Trump's inclusion on this "black" list

That organization offers its reasons in this regard. "His attacks against the press increasingly go beyond the framework of rhetoric and public policies to become physical restrictions imposed on journalists" , since he returned to the White House for a second time at the beginning of 2025.

And they add that Trump has "multiplied the attacks to reduce journalism to political communication" . They also point out that under him, the United States has dropped seven places in one year in its press freedom ranking, ending up in a rather dishonorable sixty-fourth position.

Israel Defense Forces, Chinese Communist Party or Mexican cartels

On top of all this, the report reveals that the Israel Defense Forces, the Chinese Communist Party, and the Mexican cartels, continue to be singled out as the "press predators" whom Reporters holds responsible for "a climate of terror in a supposedly 'peaceful' country" , and yet in which, so far this year, nearly one journalist has been murdered each month by organized crime.

Also included in that group of those who threaten security, and in which the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia, Mohammed bin Salman, appears, is Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.

articles.title: Costco Thanksgiving Dinner: Where you can preorder it, what is included and how much it costs
articles.standfirst: How does Costco’s package compare to other retailers such as Aldi?
articles.summary: How does Costco’s package compare to other retailers such as Aldi?
articles.body:
Costco is offering an online Thanksgiving dinner package for $199.99, providing a traditional holiday spread for up to eight people without requiring shoppers to prepare every dish from scratch as the delivery deal includes a turkey breast, multiple sides and two desserts. The Complete Gourmet Thanksgiving Turkey Dinner weighs approximately 30 pounds and costs around $25 per person, and Costco has reduced the listed price from $269.99, with delivery included, although customers will still need to cook the turkey and heat several of the accompanying dishes.

The meal is available exclusively through Costco.com , with preorders recommended by November 13. Deliveries began November 4, while orders placed by November 13 are expected to arrive by November 20. The centerpiece is a five-pound, skin-on, netted turkey breast sourced from Amish farm-raised birds. Costco describes it as free-range, antibiotic- and hormone-free, and pre-brined for preparation in the oven. The package also includes three pounds each of mashed potatoes, macaroni and cheese, sweet corn, green bean casserole and cornbread stuffing. Candied yams weigh two pounds, while the turkey gravy comes in a 24-ounce container. Cranberry relish, 12 gourmet dinner rolls, a two-pound apple cobbler and a whole pumpkin pie complete the package. Cooking instructions are provided, making the offering more convenient than sourcing and preparing every component independently. There is one important compromise for traditional turkey fans: the package contains a breast rather than a whole bird, and that means customers will not receive dark meat, legs or wings.

How Costco's price compares with Aldi, Walmart and Target

At $199.99, Costco 's package is considerably more expensive than several competing Thanksgiving offers whilst Aldi says its shopping list can feed 10 people for under $39, while Walmart has advertised a meal basket for 10 at $35. Meanwhile Target 's Thanksgiving deal is designed to feed six people for $30, and Sam's Club has advertised a feast for 16 at approximately $160 and those prices make Costco 's package a more expensive option although its delivery and preassembled selection of dishes offer a different level of convenience. Aldi 's offer requires shoppers to purchase the ingredients themselves rather than receive a prepared package as its cheaper 12-item list includes a 16-pound turkey, stuffing mix, sweet potatoes, dinner rolls, cranberries, vegetables and ingredients for pumpkin pie. Aldi has also introduced an online shopping feature that allows customers to add the listed products to a cart for pickup or delivery and chief commercial officer Scott Patton said the aim was to make holiday shopping easier and allow families to spend more time enjoying Thanksgiving .

articles.title: The heart-wrenching final audio from the Learjet 60 pilot before the crash in Florida that killed 9 people: “We’re going to crash into the ground”
articles.standfirst: The crash occurred at approximately 12:50pm local time on Sunday, November 1
articles.summary: The crash occurred at approximately 12:50pm local time on Sunday, November 1
articles.body:
The cockpit recording from a Learjet 60 's final moments reveals a desperate attempt by its crew to regain control as the aircraft plunged towards the ground in Florida , with the pilot reporting severe descent rates before warning air traffic control that a crash was imminent. Nine people aboard the private jet died when it struck the ground in Palm Springs, Palm Beach County , on Sunday afternoon after the aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was travelling to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas when it went down at approximately 12:50pm local time.

Recordings of the exchange between the cockpit and air traffic control capture the situation deteriorating rapidly as the crew initially described moderate turbulence and icing before reporting precipitation and requesting permission to climb. But within moments, the aircraft was descending at an extraordinary rate as the pilot first reported a descent of 8000 feet per minute, followed by a mayday declaration as the rate increased to 10,000 feet per minute. The crew then reported an overspeed condition and a descent of 20,000 feet per minute, before horrifyingly warning controllers, "We're gonna crash into the ground."

Final moments captured in air traffic control recording

The aircraft struck Military Trail near Cresthaven , leaving a huge crater in the roadway and debris scattered across the surrounding area as video footage appeared to show the jet descending almost vertically before erupting into a fireball, with thick smoke rising above the neighborhood. Emergency crews declared a mass casualty incident, while authorities confirmed that all nine people aboard had died. No deaths or injuries among people on the ground had been reported although approximately 600 residents from a nearby trailer-park community were evacuated. Controllers attempted to maintain communication as the emergency unfolded as one can be heard responding, "November two Bravo Delta. I'm here with you. Talk to me," whilst the pilot reported a descent of 22,000 feet and a 60-degree bank as the recording then captures an inaudible scream and the words, "Look outside." In the final exchange, air traffic control asks the crew how they can hear, but the recording provides no further clear response, which came shortly after the pilot gave a chilling update by stating, “We're out of time." The impact also damaged local infrastructure, including water lines, and officials said Military Trail could remain closed for at least 30 days. Thunderstorms had been reported in the area, with heavy rain falling during the subsequent news conference. The identities of those killed have not been released and the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating the crash, with the FAA sending a team to assist at the scene.

articles.title: Who will win the Congress race in the Midterm Elections? Predictions for the House and possible results
articles.standfirst: Voters head to the polls on Tuesday, November 3 to vote for the Republican or Democrats
articles.summary: Voters head to the polls on Tuesday, November 3 to vote for the Republican or Democrats
articles.body:
The 2026 Midterm Elections could hand Democrats control of the House of Representatives , giving them a powerful check on President Donald Trump 's final two years in office as Republican advantages on the electoral map leave the outcome uncertain. All 435 House seats are contested on November 3, and Democrats need a net gain of three to take the chamber, and Republicans currently hold 218 seats, leaving them with a narrow majority and very little room for losses.

History favors the opposition: since 1934, the president's party has lost an average of 27 House seats in midterms, making gains in only three of 23 elections whilst Trump 's declining approval adds to Republican concerns this year. Polling figures in the supplied material put Trump 's approval at around 37 percent in early October, down from just above 50 percent when he began his second term as some 61 percent of Americans disapproved of his performance. Cost-of-living pressures are central to the Democratic challenge, with voters concerned about fuel, groceries, housing and healthcare, and the war with Iran has disrupted energy supplies and pushed gasoline prices higher, adding to economic frustration. The Cook Political Report identifies 18 House districts as toss-ups, 14 currently represented by Republicans and four by Democratic Party as the Democrats could still win control without capturing any of those closely contested seats according to projections. Projections suggest that up to another 36 districts as likely or leaning Democratic – and if those forecasts hold, Democrats would have a route to a majority, although Republican redistricting and the party's campaign spending could complicate that path. Republicans have sought to improve their prospects by redrawing House districts in several states, with Democrats responding in kind and the resulting map changes have made some contests less predictable and added another variable to the national fight.

Can the Democrats win in the Senate?

The Senate presents a steeper challenge as thirty-five seats are being contested, and Democrats need a net gain of four to take control with seven races rated as toss-ups, and six currently held by Republican. Democrats must defend their Michigan seat while trying to win in states Trump carried comfortably in 2024, including Alaska , Iowa and Ohio . Texas is also a potential target, where James Talarico is challenging Republican Ken Paxton . Republicans hold a substantial financial edge: the RNC and allied groups had about $320 million in mid-October, against just under $230 million for Democrats . Trump 's MAGA Inc group had more than $160 million of its own to spend. More than $1 billion in political advertising aired during September, with Republicans spending $200 million more than Democrats and outspending them in nearly every competitive Senate race and the late push could help mobilize the red vote. The indicators suggest Democrats have a credible opportunity to win the House , but a Senate majority remains harder to reach. Either way, victory in one of the chambers would constrain Trump 's legislative agenda and enable congressional investigations.

articles.title: Zohran Mamdani, mayor of New York: "We are spending tens of billions of dollars to kill people"
articles.standfirst: The politician has criticized prioritizing military spending over social welfare
articles.summary: The politician has criticized prioritizing military spending over social welfare
articles.body:
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has given an interview to Clash Report, where he harshly criticized the military spending of the United States. The politician denounces that the U.S. government prefers to allocate tens of billions of dollars to military interventions and weaponry rather than improving public services and social rights.

“I have made clear my very deep opposition to this war in Iran. It is an opposition not only of a procedural or political nature, but, frankly, of a moral nature. We are talking about a war that has killed thousands of civilians, a war that is deeply unpopular throughout the city and across the country because it uses hundreds of billions of dollars to kill people, money that cannot be spent to make life easier for people across the country,” he said.

Mamdani: “That is not what Americans want politics to be”

Mamdani argues that prioritizing the funding of external conflicts amounts to abandoning economic and moral duties toward the working class, especially in cities suffering from high inflation and housing problems. “The things I often talk about that are necessary for working-class New Yorkers would cost a fraction of the hundreds of billions we are seeing” , he noted.

“Does it frustrate you that you are seeing this money, 900 million dollars a day, being spent on the war, when you have projects that cost much less and can make a big difference? I think it should frustrate all of us. Tupac said it decades ago and it remains true that it always seems like we have money for war, but not to feed the poor” , the mayor of New York added.

Finally, the politician proposes that those funds be used within a domestic framework to make citizens' lives easier through healthcare, education, and poverty relief, also advocating for a greater tax burden on the highest incomes. “That is not the way politics should be. That is not what Americans want politics to be” , he concluded.

articles.title: Who was Nathalia Gadelha, the 20-year-old co-pilot of the Learjet 60 that crashed near Mar-a-Lago, President Trump's residence in Florida?
articles.standfirst: The aircraft crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida and killed nine people
articles.summary: The aircraft crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida and killed nine people
articles.body:
Nathalia Gadelha was a 20-year-old pilot who earned her private pilot's license while still in high school, years before she could legally drive as she was identified by her family as the co-pilot aboard the Learjet 60 that crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida .

The aircraft was travelling from Austin, Texas , to the Bahamas when it came down near Cresthaven on Sunday afternoon, killing all nine people on board and Gadelha 's mother, Camila , and her stepfather confirmed her role.

Gadelha had grown up in Palm Beach County and attracted local attention in October 2023 after securing her pilot's license at just 17 - at the time, she was a senior at West Boca Raton High School and had yet to obtain her driver's license.

“I definitely do brag because people say, ‘Oh, you can’t drive,’ and I’m like, ‘Yeah, but I can fly,'” Gadelha told CBS12 in an interview that year and noted her interest in aviation began several years earlier.

Gadelha started taking pilot lessons in 2020, while her father also helped teach her after learning to fly recreationally in 2018 and she had accumulated 88 hours of flight time and passed the required knowledge test.

The School District of Palm Beach County's Aviation Academy funded her pilot's license after introducing its program in 2023.

Gadelha said she had flown every day since beginning ground school, describing the opportunity as something that set her apart from other students.

Gadelha dreamed of becoming a commercial airline pilot

Whilst her ambitions extended beyond earning a private license, Gadelha said that she hoped to become a commercial airline pilot, pursuing a career in aviation after developing her skills at a young age.

Despite her early achievements, Gadelha was still working towards another personal milestone when she spoke to CBS12 and she joked about the contrast between being able to operate an aircraft and not yet having a driving license.

“I just didn’t do it, and this is how it ended up,” Gadelha said. “But I think it’s cool. Some people think that it’s weird that I can fly planes, but I can’t drive a car, I mean I can but, a lot of people think it’s funny. I think it’s funny, and I now want my [driver’s] license really bad.”

She later graduated from American Flyers , a flying school based in Addison, Texas , which also operates a branch in Pompano Beach, Florida . Her family had also shared photographs on social media showing them travelling together in private aircraft.

Gadelha was among nine people killed when the Learjet 60 struck a residential area near Military Trail with investigators examining the circumstances surrounding the crash.

Air traffic control recordings captured a crew member reporting turbulence and icing before declaring an emergency, with the final cockpit message reported as: “we're out of time”.

articles.title: Powerball Winning Numbers: Results for Monday November 2 drawing for the $793 Million jackpot
articles.standfirst: Three winners claimed over a million dollars each on Saturday
articles.summary: Three winners claimed over a million dollars each on Saturday
articles.body:
The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $793 million ahead of Monday's November 2 drawing, giving players another opportunity to chase one of the biggest prizes in the lottery's history.

The winning numbers have not yet been announced though the jackpot carries an estimated cash value of $339.9 million, although the eventual winner would need to choose between that lump sum and the advertised annuity.

Monday's prize follows another drawing without a jackpot winner on Saturday, October 31 as the previous draw produced the numbers 2, 4, 18, 50 and 56, alongside the red Powerball 20.

The Power Play multiplier was 3X, while three tickets secured substantial prizes without matching all six numbers as one ticket sold in Georgia and another in the United Kingdom matched the five main numbers to win $1 million each.

Additionally, another North Carolina player also matched those numbers and used Power Play, turning the prize into $2 million.

What to know about the $793 million Powerball drawing

Monday's jackpot is now larger than the $768.4 million prize won in Wisconsin in 2019, placing it above the 10th-largest Powerball jackpot on record. The top prize remains subject to change if ticket sales push the final amount higher.

The drawing is scheduled for 22:59 ET/19:59 PT, with Powerball numbers selected every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday. Players choose five numbers from 1 to 69 and one red Powerball from 1 to 26, either selecting them themselves or using a quick-pick option.

A standard ticket costs $2, while the chance of matching all six numbers and winning the jackpot stands at 1 in 292.2 million. Power Play costs an additional $1 and can multiply non-jackpot prizes, but it does not increase the jackpot.

Powerball is available in 45 states, Washington D.C. and the US Virgin Islands . Players do not need to be US citizens or residents to take part, although ticket sales cut-off times and purchasing options vary depending on the jurisdiction.

Online purchases are permitted in several locations, including Kentucky , Connecticut , Georgia , Illinois , Kansas , Michigan , New Hampshire , North Carolina , North Dakota , Pennsylvania , Virginia , West Virginia and Washington D.C . Some states also use third-party services for online ticket purchases.

The Double Play option provides another chance to win, with a separate drawing and a top prize of $10 million. It costs an additional $1 where available, including in Kentucky and Indiana , and has its own set of numbers.

Saturday's Double Play draw produced 16, 52, 55, 58 and 67, with the red number 24. Monday's main drawing will determine whether a ticketholder claims the $793 million jackpot or the prize rolls over again.

articles.title: Thanksgiving 2026: When is it and what to know before traveling, shopping or celebrating?
articles.standfirst: An important holiday is just around the corner.
articles.summary: An important holiday is just around the corner.
articles.body:
November is here, and with it comes the countdown to one of the year's most anticipated celebrations. Thanksgiving is getting closer, and between traveling to reunite with family, preparing the holiday dinner and making plans for the long weekend , there are several details worth keeping in mind to avoid any last-minute surprises.

This year, Thanksgiving will be celebrated on Thursday, November 26, kicking off a weekend that will also feature the traditional Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade and Black Friday deals . If you're already making plans, here are the dates and details you should know.

Which days will see the most traffic on roads and at airports?

As happens every year, the days leading up to Thanksgiving will account for a large share of holiday travel. Tuesday, November 24, and Wednesday, November 25, will be two of the busiest dates for those heading out before the holiday . Traffic is also expected to pick up on Sunday, November 29, as many people make their way home after spending time with family or taking a few days away.

If you're still planning your itinerary, it's best to compare transportation options and check flight schedules ahead of time. Traveling on Thursday, November 26, itself could be an alternative for those looking to avoid some of the busiest travel days , although that doesn't guarantee cheaper fares or less crowded airports.

Weather conditions should also be part of your preparations, especially if you're planning to drive or connect through other cities. Preliminary forecasts point to changing conditions across several regions of the United States, including falling temperatures, rain and possible snowfall in parts of the North and East . Checking local forecasts before leaving can help you prepare for unexpected changes along the way.

Will Walmart and Target be open on Thanksgiving 2026?

If you're thinking about leaving some shopping until the last minute, there's something important you should know: Walmart and Target will keep their stores closed on Thursday, November 26. That means you won't be able to visit either retailer to pick up missing dinner ingredients or take care of any last-minute errands during the holiday.

The best option is to do your grocery shopping ahead of time and make sure you have everything you need for dinner, from ingredients and drinks to those final details for the gathering. If something unexpected comes up, you can check the hours of other nearby stores, as each retailer sets its own Thanksgiving schedule.

Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade 2026: Start Time and Route in New York City

While families across the country get ready for their holiday dinners, another major Thanksgiving tradition will be getting underway early in New York City. The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade will once again fill the streets of Manhattan.

The parade will begin at 8:30 a.m. on Thursday, November 26, and is expected to wrap up around noon. It will start at 77th Street and Central Park West , near the American Museum of Natural History. From there, it will travel along Central Park West, pass the Central Park South area and continue down Sixth Avenue before reaching Herald Square, in front of Macy's at 34th Street.

When Is Black Friday 2026?

And as if Thanksgiving weren't already reason enough to celebrate, the holiday weekend will continue with another of November's most anticipated dates for shoppers. Black Friday will take place on Friday, November 27, with deals available at brick-and-mortar stores and online retailers .

If you're planning to get a head start on your Christmas shopping or finally buy something you've had your eye on, comparing prices before making a decision can help you find a good deal.

articles.title: Musk breaks the bank by donating nearly $500 million to Republicans for the United States elections
articles.standfirst: The billionaire sets a historic record with his contribution
articles.summary: The billionaire sets a historic record with his contribution
articles.body:
Elon Musk has once again placed himself at the center of the political spotlight in the United States. The owner of Tesla, SpaceX and X has become the largest known donor in a single election cycle in the country's history after allocating 474 million dollars to organizations linked to the Republican Party ahead of the legislative elections being held this Tuesday.

The figure is unprecedented for a person who is not running as a candidate in the elections. According to an investigation by The New York Times, the volume of the magnate's contributions surpasses any previously known record . In addition, the amount could be even higher , since some of his donations are not public and federal records only reflect the transactions made up to last October 14 .

The billionaire has channeled these funds to strengthen the Republican strategy in a key election for control of Congress. While conservatives are trying to hold on to their majority, Democrats are seeking to regain ground in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Musk's economic involvement is total and comes accompanied by growing political pressure. Several Democratic lawmakers have already warned that they will push for investigations into the businessman if they manage to gain control of either of the two chambers.

Possible investigations would focus on different fronts: from his management at the helm of the now-defunct Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), to his companies' public contracts and his role in matters related to the war between Russia and Ukraine.

Historic spending in these midterm elections

Musk's record coincides with a campaign that is also shattering political investment figures in the United States. Data from the specialized firm AdImpact show that the 2026 midterm elections have reached historic levels of advertising spending, surpassing even the records set by the 2024 presidential elections.

In a scenario marked by the battle for Congress and by the growing weight of major donors, Musk’s entry with nearly $500 million further strengthens his influence in U.S. politics and makes him one of the most decisive players in the current electoral cycle.

articles.title: Who is Erin Benavides, the woman linked to Tony Parker and Eva Longoria's divorce, whose chilling suicide has reignited the scandal?
articles.standfirst: Benavides’ death has reopened old wounds between Parker and Longoria
articles.summary: Benavides’ death has reopened old wounds between Parker and Longoria
articles.body:
The death of Erin Benavides has brought fresh attention to the events behind Tony Parker and Eva Longoria 's divorce, more than 15 years after their marriage collapsed amid reports of messages between the former NBA star and another woman. Benavides , previously known as Erin Barry , died by suicide at her home in Port Aransas, Texas , on October 14 and she was reportedly identified as the woman linked to Parker in the controversy that engulfed both families in 2010.

A police report witnessed by Page Six has revealed that officers discovered three firearms and multiple bullets inside the property after authorities had been alerted by a call at approximately 19:08 CT from someone reporting that a woman had threatened to take her own life. Police forced entry into the home and found Benavides with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, and investigators have said they do not suspect foul play as the investigation remains ongoing. The circumstances of her death have revived interest in a scandal that involved two high-profile marriages. At the time, Benavides was married to Brent Barry , a former San Antonio Spurs player and teammate of Parker , who was married to Desperate Housewives actress Longoria .

The allegations that brought two marriages to an end

The November 2010 after reports that Longoria had discovered hundreds of text messages between Parker and another woman, and Benavides was subsequently identified in media coverage as the person involved in the exchanges. However, the allegations were disputed as Benavides denied having an affair with Parker , whilst the former Spurs guard reportedly denied that the pair had a physical relationship. The messages nevertheless became a major focus of coverage as both marriages unraveled after Parker and Longoria had first met in 2004 before beginning a relationship the following year. They announced their engagement in November 2006 and married in Paris in July 2007, with a civil ceremony followed by a lavish celebration at a French chateau and Longoria was a familiar presence at Spurs games during Parker 's playing career as the couple became one of the most recognizable pairings in American entertainment and sport. They had no children together, and their marriage lasted just over three years before Longoria filed for divorce in Los Angeles on November 17, 2010, citing irreconcilable differences. She requested that her name be restored to Eva Jacqueline Longoria . Parker later filed his own petition, citing discord or conflict of personalities and Benavides ' life subsequently took a different direction from the celebrity headlines as she became a Texas prosecutor, working on human-smuggling cases and advocating for vulnerable children. She resigned from her position in August, around two months before her death and her professional career and earlier connection to Parker have now become part of the renewed public focus on her life. The allegations from 2010, however, were never established as fact, and her death does not resolve the disputed claims surrounding the two marriages.

articles.title: The tragic final message from young pilot Nathalia Gadelha is revealed following the horrific accident in Florida that left 9 people dead
articles.standfirst: The 20-year-old co-pilot reportedly warned about turbulence and ice just 10 minutes before the aircraft plunged to the ground
articles.summary: The 20-year-old co-pilot reportedly warned about turbulence and ice just 10 minutes before the aircraft plunged to the ground
articles.body:
Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras was living out her dream of becoming a professional pilot when a devastating aircraft accident in Florida claimed her life alongside eight others and now, a heartbreaking message sent to her boyfriend shortly before the crash has emerged. The 20-year-old was serving as co-pilot aboard a Learjet 60 that crashed in Palm Beach County on Sunday, November 1, killing everyone on board and the new offering a glimpse into the terrifying conditions aboard the aircraft.

According to her stepfather, Thiago Corteleti , Gadelha contacted her boyfriend, who is also a pilot, shortly before the disaster. "She texted her boyfriend, I think, at 12:40 p.m. and the accident was at 12:50 p.m.," the 44-year-old Corteleti told The New York Post as her message reportedly contained just a few words, but they would take on heartbreaking significance following the tragedy. "She just said, 'I've got turbulence, I've got ice,'" her stepfather recalled Gadelha saying as the communication came as the aircraft encountered increasingly difficult conditions during its journey from Austin, Texas , towards the Bahamas . Air traffic control recordings subsequently captured the crew reporting icing and turbulence before declaring an emergency. All nine occupants were killed when the aircraft crashed, with investigators now examining the circumstances surrounding its rapid descent.

Nathalia Gadelha had already logged 1300 flying hours

Despite being just 20, Gadelha had already built considerable experience in aviation and was pursuing her ambition of becoming a commercial airline pilot after she obtained her private pilot's license in October 2023, aged just 17, while attending West Boca Raton High School . Her achievement attracted attention from local media, particularly because she had not yet obtained her driver's license and she boasted about gaining her wings before being allowed to handle four wheels on a road. By the time of Sunday's accident, Gadelha had reportedly accumulated more than 1,300 flight hours and had been working as a commercial pilot for approximately nine months. She had also trained at American Flyers , a flight school headquartered in Addison, Texas , which operates a location in Pompano Beach, Florida and her social media frequently featured photographs and videos of her flying. Footage including her boyfriend Justin , with whom she shared an interest in aviation and Gadelha had previously highlighted how unusual it was for two pilots under the age of 21 to hold commercial, multi-engine, instrument and flight instructor qualifications. The loss has devastated her family, particularly her mother, Regina , who admitted she had long worried that her daughter's passion for flying could ultimately separate them. "I wanted her to live her dream, but I knew that her dream was going to be the thing that would take her away from me," Regina told The New York Post. "I knew that a plane was gonna take her away from me. I always knew it, but I was so proud of her. I know she was living her dream."

articles.title: What are the Social Security projected benefit cuts for 2032? This is how much benefits may be reduced
articles.standfirst: Millions of Americans could face a significant reduction in their retirement payments within six years
articles.summary: Millions of Americans could face a significant reduction in their retirement payments within six years
articles.body:
Social Security is approaching a financial deadline that could have serious consequences for millions of retired Americans , with projections suggesting benefits may be reduced by more than one-fifth in 2032 unless lawmakers agree on a solution.

According to the 2026 Social Security Trustees Report , the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance (OASI) Trust Fund , which finances retirement and survivor benefits, is projected to exhaust its accumulated reserves in the fourth quarter of 2032.

If Congress does not intervene, the government would no longer have sufficient dedicated funding to pay the full benefits promised under current law as the trustees estimate that incoming revenue would cover approximately 78% of scheduled payments.

Leaving beneficiaries facing an automatic 22% reduction, the Congressional Budget Office has offered an even more concerning forecast, projecting that the retirement trust fund could become depleted by mid-2032.

Its estimates suggest retirees could face benefit reductions of approximately 26% and the potential financial consequences are substantial, particularly for older Americans who depend heavily on their monthly Social Security payments to cover everyday expenses.

How much could Social Security payments be reduced?

The impact would vary depending on how much each individual currently receives, but estimates suggest the reductions could amount to hundreds of dollars every month and according to a June report from the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget , an estimated 24% reduction would translate into an average monthly benefit cut of approximately $500 nationwide.

Retirees in 29 states could experience even larger average reductions, highlighting how the potential changes could affect households differently depending on their existing benefit payments.

A reduction of that size could make it considerably harder for retirees to afford housing, groceries, healthcare and other essential expenses, particularly those without substantial savings or additional retirement income.

However, Social Security would not disappear when its retirement trust fund runs out of reserves and workers would continue paying payroll taxes, meaning the program would still collect revenue and distribute benefits.

The problem is that the money coming into the system would no longer be sufficient to cover the full amount currently scheduled for beneficiaries.

The financial difficulties are largely connected to demographic changes across the United States as Social Security was established in 1935 and relies primarily on payroll taxes collected from employees and employers.

Its financial structure depends on workers contributing money to support retirees, disabled individuals and qualifying family members. However, Americans are living longer, while the large baby-boomer generation has increasingly moved into retirement.

At the same time, declining birth rates have reduced the growth of the younger workforce responsible for supporting the program. This means more people are collecting benefits for longer periods, while the number of taxpayers falls.

articles.title: When will we know the results of the Midterm Elections? Possible time of the final numbers in today's race
articles.standfirst: Voters head to the polls on Tuesday, November 3 to vote Republican or Democrat
articles.summary: Voters head to the polls on Tuesday, November 3 to vote Republican or Democrat
articles.body:
Polls close across the United States on Tuesday, but the fight for control of Congress may continue long after the first results arrive, leaving the country waiting for a decisive answer although election night will not deliver one definitive moment when Americans learns who has won the midterms.

The first returns should follow the opening poll closures at 18:00 ET/15:00 PT, but control of Congress could remain unsettled long after voting ends as every House of Representatives seat, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships are being contested, consuming a substantial amount of time to collect and ratify votes.

Democrats need net gains of three House seats and four Senate seats to take Congress , potentially limiting Trump 's agenda during his final two years in office and DDHQ 's latest forecast puts Democrats ' chances of winning the House at 84 percent and the Senate at 65 percent.

North Carolina , Alaska , Maine , Texas and Ohio are among the Senate contests drawing attention, but forecasts are not results, and the first indication will come as polls begin closing from 18:00 Eastern Time and continue through to as last as midnight ET in Alaska .

Those deadlines end voting, not counting. States have different rules for processing mail ballots and provisional votes, and election offices report at different speeds. Close margins can leave outstanding ballots decisive after most votes are in.

Why the final count could stretch beyond election night

Historically, Florida , Georgia , North Carolina and Texas are expected to report substantial totals relatively quickly whilst Michigan , Wisconsin and Pennsylvania may take longer, as ballot-processing rules can delay mail vote reporting.

Contests decided by narrow margins can also cause delays if recounts are issued and some states such as California may also keep some races open for days or weeks as the state accepts mail ballots postmarked by Election Day for up to seven days afterward, and those ballots require checks before they can be included in the count.

The margin and the amount of outstanding voting can matter more than the speed of reporting whilst Decision Desk HQ says it projects a winner only when it is 99.9999 percent confident but that is not official certification and it's possible they can be upset.

Election officials must complete their canvass, and experts say every state takes weeks to certify its election results meaning there is therefore no guaranteed hour for the final congressional picture.

Some winners may be projected Tuesday night, but control of either chamber could remain unclear on Wednesday if a small number of close races determine the majority.

Newly elected members of Congress are scheduled to take office at 12:00 ET/09:00 PT on January 3.

Certain special Senate election winners may be sworn in sooner, while state and local officeholders follow dates set by their respective laws.

articles.title: Mega Millions winning numbers: Results for this Tuesday November 3 drawing for the $482 million jackpot
articles.standfirst: Nobody managed to claim the prize in the previous drawing on October 30
articles.summary: Nobody managed to claim the prize in the previous drawing on October 30
articles.body:
The Mega Millions jackpot is estimated at $482 million ahead of Tuesday night's drawing, giving players another opportunity to win one of the largest lottery prizes currently available in the United States . The winning numbers have not yet been announced but the November 3 drawing is scheduled for 23:00 ET/20:00 PT and the results will only be available after the draw takes place.

The previous drawing took place on Friday, October 30, when the numbers drawn were 5, 10, 38, 49 and 68 , with 17 selected as the Mega Ball as no ticket matched all six numbers, allowing the jackpot to roll over. Tuesday's advertised top prize is $482 million, while the estimated cash option stands at $203.6 million before taxes and the annuity value is paid through a series of annual instalments, rather than as one immediate payment. The jackpot has been building since July 28, when a ticket sold at a Wawa store in Bradenton, Florida , won an estimated $800 million - but that prize had a cash value of $344.2 million, before applicable taxes. Since that Florida win, consecutive drawings have passed without another jackpot winner, and each rollover adds to the prize pool and can draw wider attention as the advertised total approaches the half-billion-dollar mark.

How to play Mega Millions and check the November 3 results

Each Mega Millions play costs $5 as players select five white-ball numbers from 1 to 70 and one gold Mega Ball number from 1 to 24 and those who prefer not to choose can request a Quick Pick and receive randomly generated numbers. Every ticket now includes a multiplier, assigned automatically, which can increase non-jackpot prizes by two, three, four, five or 10 times whilst the multiplier does not apply to the jackpot, and the prize depends on the numbers matched. The odds of winning the jackpot are approximately one in 290.5 million, while the overall odds of winning any prize are around one in 23 as the game offers nine prize tiers, with non-jackpot awards ranging from $10 to $10 million. Mega Millions drawings take place every Tuesday and Friday at 23:00 ET/20:00 PT and the official winning numbers and drawing video are posted on the game's website shortly after each draw, once the results are available. Players should compare all six numbers on their ticket with the official results and check the multiplier printed on the ticket, and lottery authorities advise winners to have tickets validated through an authorized retailer or their state lottery. With the November 3 drawing still ahead, the $482 million jackpot remains available to be won. If no ticket matches all six numbers, the prize will roll over again and the next estimated jackpot will be announced after the draw.

articles.title: Living the dream: A look inside the idyllic life of millionaire tycoon Adam Robinson and his family before the tragic plane crash in Florida
articles.standfirst: Friends reveal how the businessman was enjoying a dream life with his family just days before the devastating Florida crash
articles.summary: Friends reveal how the businessman was enjoying a dream life with his family just days before the devastating Florida crash
articles.body:
The life of technology entrepreneur Adam Robinson appeared to be reaching an extraordinary high point just days before a devastating plane crash claimed the lives of him and his family.

The 45-year-old businessman, his wife Helen Sharp and their two children, Emma , four, and Charlie , two, were travelling to the Bahamas for a birthday celebration when tragedy struck in Florida .

According to a friend, Robinson had recently spoken enthusiastically about how well everything was going. His companies were expanding, and family life in Aspen, Colorado, was bringing him considerable happiness.

He reportedly described things as “going too well”, an observation that has taken on a heartbreaking significance following the crash.

Friend Jesse Ouellette described him as an incredible person whose influence reached across the software start-up community.

"He challenged the way things were done and was far ahead of his time. It's heartbreaking that we lost him so soon,” he told TMZ.

Robinson built a reputation through his work developing software businesses. He co-founded email marketing company Robly before going on to establish ventures including Retention.com, RB2B and MoltSets.

His approach to entrepreneurship focused on building sustainable companies, challenging conventional thinking and finding opportunities without necessarily relying on outside investment.

A successful career and a close-knit family

Away from the business world, Robinson's family was at the center of his happiness. He and Helen shared a life that included time in Aspen, where they enjoyed raising their two young children.

Their family appeared to be embracing an exciting chapter, with Robinson balancing his growing business interests with the pleasures of parenthood.

In a statement following the tragedy, relatives remembered Adam and Helen as devoted parents, describing their children as the light of their lives. The loss has left friends and colleagues struggling to understand how a family with so much to look forward to could be taken so suddenly.

The family had set off from Austin on November 1 aboard a Learjet 60, bound for North Eleuthera in the Bahamas. They were accompanied by friends Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr , their nanny Anita Maria Cetina and two pilots, Captain Jeff Gregory and co-pilot Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras . All nine people aboard died when the aircraft crashed in Palm Beach County.

Investigators have begun piecing together the jet's final moments. The National Transportation Safety Board said the crew reported icing and moderate turbulence at around 35,000 feet before requesting permission to climb.

Less than 30 seconds after clearance was granted, the aircraft began descending rapidly and a mayday call followed.

Officials are examining weather conditions and other evidence to establish what happened. However, no definitive cause has been established, and the investigation remains ongoing.

Robinson's legacy will live on through the businesses he built, the founders he encouraged and the family and friends whose lives he touched.

articles.title: November 2026 astronomical events you won't want to miss
articles.standfirst: These are the dates worth marking on your calendar.
articles.summary: These are the dates worth marking on your calendar.
articles.body:
The year is entering its final stretch, but the night sky still has plenty of surprises in store. Throughout November 2026, stargazers will have several opportunities to look up and witness something special, from meteor showers and a particularly large-looking Full Moon to planetary gatherings.

The best part? You won't have to wait for just one date to enjoy the show . Several celestial events will take place throughout the month, some visible to the naked eye and others easier to spot with the help of binoculars.

The first event to watch for will be the Southern Taurids, a meteor shower expected to reach its peak between November 4 and 5 . Although its activity is usually modest, producing around five to 10 meteors per hour, it has one feature that makes it special: it can produce fireballs, exceptionally bright flashes that streak across the sky and stand out even when only a few meteors appear.

To catch them, find a location away from city lights and give your eyes time to adjust to the darkness. You won't need a telescope. Observing with the naked eye will allow you to take in a much wider area of the sky.

A few days later, it will be time for the Northern Taurids . This meteor shower will also have relatively modest activity, with approximately five meteors per hour, making patience your best ally.

Although it isn't one of the most active meteor showers, it's still worth keeping an eye on the sky throughout the night and into the early morning hours. Remember that shooting stars can appear in different directions, so there's no need to focus on just one spot.

Four planets will appear before sunrise

Starting November 13, another highlight of the month will begin: Mercury, Venus, Mars and Jupiter will appear spread across the sky before sunrise . This planetary display will continue through November 22.

Although it's often described as an alignment, that doesn't mean the planets will form a straight line in space. From our perspective on Earth, they will simply appear in the same region of the sky. To spot them, look for a clear view of the eastern horizon and head outside before sunrise.

Another date worth marking is November 17-18, when the Leonids will reach their peak . This meteor shower is known for the speed of its meteors, which travel through Earth's atmosphere at tremendous speeds and can leave behind striking flashes of light.

The best time to look for them will be during the early morning hours of November 18, after midnight, when the constellation Leo will be better positioned for viewing. As with other meteor showers, your best bet is to find a dark location and keep your eyes on a wide area of the sky.

As part of the planetary display, there will be a special date for anyone hoping to spot Mercury. On November 20, the planet will reach its greatest western elongation, meaning it will appear at its farthest point from the Sun in the sky from our perspective.

This position will offer one of the best opportunities during this period to observe the planet. Look toward the eastern horizon shortly before sunrise, when Mercury should still be visible above the horizon.

One of the month's most anticipated events will arrive on November 24 with the Beaver Supermoon. The Full Moon will occur close to perigee, the point in its orbit when it is closest to Earth . As a result, it may appear slightly larger and brighter than an average Full Moon.

One of the best times to enjoy the view will be as the Moon rises above the eastern horizon around sunset.

The Moon will also be near the Pleiades star cluster that same date, adding another beautiful feature to the night sky.

A day later, on November 25, Uranus will reach opposition, a position in which Earth lies directly between the planet and the Sun . This means Uranus will be visible for much of the night, making it a favorable time to observe the distant planet.

Uranus will appear in the region of the constellation Taurus. Although it may be close to the naked-eye visibility limit under exceptionally dark skies, binoculars will make it much easier to find. Unlike brighter planets such as Venus and Jupiter, spotting Uranus will require a little more patience.

November will wrap up its astronomical calendar with another eye-catching gathering. On November 30, the Moon, Jupiter, Mars and the star Regulus will appear close together in the sky , occupying a region of approximately 5.2 degrees.

The grouping should be visible to the naked eye, weather permitting and provided the horizon is clear. It will be a great opportunity to spot several celestial objects in the same area of the sky and end the month with one more special stargazing moment.

articles.title: Tom Brady's former TV admirer Inés Gómez Mont arrested amid $160 million fraud allegations
articles.summary: Mexican television presenter Inés Gómez Mont, 43, was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Florida on October 30, 2026, after spending five years wanted by Mexican authorities. She and her husband, lawyer Víctor Manuel Álvarez Puga, face allegations involving organized crime, money laundering, tax fraud, and the alleged diversion of approximately $160 million in public funds through shell companies and fraudulent government contracts.
articles.body:
Mexican television presenter Inés Gómez Mont, 43, was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Florida on October 30, 2026, after spending five years wanted by Mexican authorities. She and her husband, lawyer Víctor Manuel Álvarez Puga, face allegations involving organized crime, money laundering, tax fraud, and the alleged diversion of approximately $160 million in public funds through shell companies and fraudulent government contracts.

Gómez Mont became internationally known in 2008 when she appeared at Super Bowl Media Day wearing a wedding dress and playfully proposed to then-New England Patriots quarterback Tom Brady, who declined.

Mexican prosecutors have confirmed three outstanding arrest warrants against her. Gómez Mont remains in U.S. immigration custody while authorities consider her immigration status and possible return to Mexico. She has consistently denied wrongdoing and maintains her innocence.

articles.title: Donald Trump could face a historic constitutional test after Democrats’ projected sweep, but Republicans may hold the key
articles.standfirst: Election projections could give Democrats a chance to revive a commission proposal
articles.summary: Election projections could give Democrats a chance to revive a commission proposal
articles.body:
A change in Congress could bring a rarely used constitutional provision back into focus. The 25th Amendment’s Section 4 has never been invoked, and Democrats have proposed a commission that could examine whether a president is unable to carry out the duties of the office. But even if election projections hold, a Democratic majority would not be enough to put the plan into effect or transfer power from President Donald Trump.

Rep. Jamie Raskin introduced the commission bill, H.R. 8275, in April. It was referred to the House Judiciary and Rules committees and has not become law. The proposal would create a 17-member panel: eight physicians, including four psychiatrists; eight former senior executive branch officials; and a chair. Congress could direct the commission to examine the president.

A commission could assess incapacity, but it could not act alone

Section 4 requires the vice president and a majority of either the Cabinet or a congressionally established body to jointly declare that the president is unable to perform the duties of the office. If that declaration is sent to Congress, the vice president immediately assumes those powers as acting president. The amendment does not remove the president from office.

That makes Vance central to any Section 4 effort. If Trump contests the declaration, the vice president and a majority of the Cabinet or commission have four days to reaffirm it.

Congress then has 21 days to decide the issue. The president remains unable to exercise the powers of the office only if two-thirds of both chambers vote to sustain the declaration; otherwise, he resumes them.

There is another major hurdle: the commission must first be established by law. That means a bill would need to pass both chambers and go to Trump to sign. If he vetoed it, Congress would need two-thirds support in each chamber to override him. A projected Democratic majority would not, by itself, establish the commission.

The medical claims need careful handling

Raskin has argued that Trump’s public statements raise concerns about his capacity. Those are the sponsor’s stated reasons for the bill, not a medical finding.

The claims in the supplied material about neurological decline, speech and movements should not be presented as established proof of incapacity: the commission does not exist and has not examined Trump.

The White House physician’s report from May said Trump was in “excellent health” and “fully fit” to serve.

paragraphs: A change in Congress could bring a rarely used constitutional provision back into focus. The 25th Amendment’s Section 4 has never been invoked, and Democrats have proposed a commission that could examine whether a president is unable to carry out the duties of the office. But even if election projections hold, a Democratic majority would not be enough to put the plan into effect or transfer power from President Donald Trump.

Rep. Jamie Raskin introduced the commission bill, H.R. 8275, in April. It was referred to the House Judiciary and Rules committees and has not become law. The proposal would create a 17-member panel: eight physicians, including four psychiatrists; eight former senior executive branch officials; and a chair. Congress could direct the commission to examine the president.
A commission could assess incapacity, but it could not act alone

Section 4 requires the vice president and a majority of either the Cabinet or a congressionally established body to jointly declare that the president is unable to perform the duties of the office. If that declaration is sent to Congress, the vice president immediately assumes those powers as acting president. The amendment does not remove the president from office.
That makes Vance central to any Section 4 effort. If Trump contests the declaration, the vice president and a majority of the Cabinet or commission have four days to reaffirm it.

Congress then has 21 days to decide the issue. The president remains unable to exercise the powers of the office only if two-thirds of both chambers vote to sustain the declaration; otherwise, he resumes them.

There is another major hurdle: the commission must first be established by law. That means a bill would need to pass both chambers and go to Trump to sign. If he vetoed it, Congress would need two-thirds support in each chamber to override him. A projected Democratic majority would not, by itself, establish the commission.
The medical claims need careful handling
Raskin has argued that Trump’s public statements raise concerns about his capacity. Those are the sponsor’s stated reasons for the bill, not a medical finding.

The claims in the supplied material about neurological decline, speech and movements should not be presented as established proof of incapacity: the commission does not exist and has not examined Trump.
The White House physician’s report from May said Trump was in “excellent health” and “fully fit” to serve.

Election projections may change which proposals Congress chooses to take up when the new session begins. They do not activate Section 4. For that to happen, lawmakers would first have to pass a law, and Vance would still have to join the declaration.
The constitutional question is not simply whether Congress can investigate a president; it is whether the president is unable to do the job and Section 4 sets a high bar for answering it.
