articles.title: VA Unemployment Benefits: How much can you get and who is eligible to apply for extra benefits?
articles.standfirst: Former service members unable to work because of qualifying disabilities may receive compensation at the 100% rate
articles.summary: Former service members unable to work because of qualifying disabilities may receive compensation at the 100% rate
articles.body:
Veterans struggling to maintain employment because of disabilities connected to their military service may qualify for significantly higher federal payments, even if they have never received a 100% disability rating.

The Department of Veterans Affairs offers financial assistance through Individual Unemployability , a program that allows qualifying former service members to receive compensation at the highest standard disability rate when their medical conditions prevent them from holding steady employment.

Under the 2026 payment schedule, eligible veterans without dependents can receive $3,938.58 per month, equivalent to $47,262.96 annually. Those with qualifying family members may be entitled to additional compensation.

However, receiving these payments isn't automatic. Applicants must demonstrate that their inability to work results from disabilities connected to their military service, rather than unemployment caused by economic conditions or other circumstances.

That is particularly important because the VA's Individual Unemployability program operates separately from traditional unemployment insurance available to former military personnel.

Who is eligible for VA Individual Unemployability benefits?

Veterans generally qualify for consideration when they have at least one service-connected disability rated at 60% or higher that prevents them from maintaining substantially gainful employment.

Those with multiple service-connected conditions may also qualify if their combined disability rating reaches 70%, provided at least one condition carries an individual rating of 40% or higher.

The VA can consider exceptional cases involving lower disability ratings when medical evidence establishes that service-connected conditions prevent suitable employment.

Applicants don't necessarily need to be completely unemployed. Occasional work or employment classified as marginal may be permitted without automatically disqualifying them.

Importantly, approval doesn't increase a veteran's official disability rating to 100%. Instead, their monthly compensation rises to the equivalent payment level while the underlying disability rating remains unchanged.

Veterans seeking these benefits must submit VA Form 21-8940, alongside employment information requested through Form 21-4192, and provide supporting evidence demonstrating how their disabilities affect their ability to work.

How much can veterans receive through unemployment assistance?

Former military personnel who become unemployed after leaving active duty may qualify for a separate federal program known as Unemployment Compensation for Ex-servicemembers , or UCX.

Unlike VA Individual Unemployability , UCX provides temporary financial assistance administered through state unemployment agencies, with payment amounts determined by the state handling the application.

Eligible applicants generally must have completed qualifying military service, received an honorable discharge and satisfied the relevant state's unemployment requirements.

There's no universal nationwide weekly payment for UCX. Both the amount available and the duration of assistance depend on applicable state rules and qualifying military earnings.

Veterans should contact their state workforce agency promptly after separation and have their DD-214 discharge documentation available when applying.

Those pursuing disability-related Individual Unemployability benefits should apply directly through the VA, which can also provide guidance through its benefits helpline at 800-827-1000.

Understanding which program applies can make a substantial difference, particularly for veterans whose service-connected conditions have left them unable to maintain a reliable income.

articles.title: Christa Pike, the woman who survived two execution attempts, faces a new health problem
articles.standfirst: The inmate, sentenced to death in the United States, suffers from a blood disorder linked to a rare form of cancer and is now seeking protection for fear of suffering further assaults in the penitentiary center
articles.summary: The inmate, sentenced to death in the United States, suffers from a blood disorder linked to a rare form of cancer and is now seeking protection for fear of suffering further assaults in the penitentiary center
articles.body:
The story of Christa Pike is once again drawing international attention due to the combination of her medical problems , the circumstances under which she survived the execution, and the conditions in which she remains imprisoned. According to the New York Post , her lawyers had already warned months earlier that her blood disorders could increase the risks of a lethal injection .

Pike, 50, remains in custody at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Tennessee. She was transferred there after being hospitalized for ten days following the failed September 30 procedure, when she received two doses of pentobarbital , the drug used by authorities to carry out the death penalty .

A blood disorder that had already raised alarm bells

The information published by the New York Post indicates that Pike suffers from a myeloproliferative disorder, a rare disease that affects the production of blood cells and that may be associated with the development of blood cancer. Her legal representatives had mentioned this condition in a document filed with the courts in January 2026, before the execution procedure was carried out.

In that filing, the attorneys also noted that the inmate had thrombocytosis, a disorder characterized by an elevated level of platelets in the blood . According to her defense’s arguments, this condition could increase the risk of complications during the administration of the drugs, including pulmonary edema, which consists of the accumulation of fluid in the lungs and can cause breathing difficulties and a sensation of suffocation .

The defense had also warned about Pike’s history of difficulties with blood draws and the placement of intravenous needles. These problems became especially relevant during the attempted execution in September. Nevertheless, it is important to clarify that the documentation cited by the media records the medical arguments presented by her lawyers and does not allow, on its own, establishing that there is independent medical confirmation of the cancer diagnosis .

She survived two doses of lethal injection in Tennessee

On September 30, 2026, Pike was supposed to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than two centuries. However, the procedure ended unexpectedly: prison officials administered two doses of pentobarbital to her, but the woman remained alive and had to be rushed to a hospital .

According to court documents cited by Associated Press and the Death Penalty Information Center, the team in charge of the execution had difficulty finding a vein and inserting the IV lines. The lawyers argued that officials used around ten needles and took nearly an hour to establish a suitable line . During the procedure, Pike reported pain in one of her arms and later experienced difficulty breathing.

The inmate remained unconscious and in critical condition, with significant injuries to her arms. After several days of medical care, she regained consciousness and was able to communicate again. On October 10, she was discharged and transferred back to the penitentiary . Tennessee Governor Bill Lee ordered an independent investigation into what happened and suspended the executions scheduled in the state for the remainder of 2026 .

The fear of returning to the unit where she witnessed assaults

Pike's new problem has to do with the place authorities could transfer her to once her recovery is complete. According to NTN24, the woman filed a legal request to prevent her from being returned to the maximum-security unit where she was held before the execution attempt . In her petition, she said that she fears suffering new assaults because she believes that her current physical condition makes her especially vulnerable.

"I fear being seriously injured if I am transferred to that unit while so weak" , Pike stated in the document filed by her lawyers. She also asserted that during the two years she remained in that sector, she witnessed attacks between inmates and against prison staff, as well as incidents involving prisoners with severe psychological problems. The defense also described poor hygienic conditions, with showers infested with insects.

According to Noticias de Navarra, El Tiempo and information reported by Fox News, her legal representatives also question that she remains isolated in the prison infirmary . They maintain that this situation affects her mental health and contradicts a 2024 court agreement that allowed her to work and interact with other inmates. For now , authorities are keeping Pike in the medical area while her recovery continues .

A case that once again puts the death penalty under scrutiny

Pike’s situation also has legal implications. Her attorneys believe that the failed execution attempt may have violated the constitutional prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment . For that reason, a Tennessee court ordered the preservation of evidence related to the procedure, including the medications, syringes, intravenous equipment, and audiovisual records that may help clarify what happened.

Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer, a 19-year-old young woman whom she attended a job training center with in Knoxville. The crime occurred in January 1995, when Pike was 18 years old, and it also involved her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp. The woman was found guilty of first-degree murder and later received an additional 25-year sentence for an attempted murder against another inmate in prison.

Thirty years after that crime, Pike remains on death row, but her future is uncertain . While her lawyers seek guarantees regarding her medical care and conditions of confinement, Tennessee authorities have kept the executions scheduled for this year suspended . The investigation into the September 30 procedure and the new court filings will be crucial to determining what will happen to the woman who survived two doses of lethal injection .

articles.title: Who is Miguel Ángel Urbano Vázquez? The Mexican "monster" who spread terror in the United States
articles.standfirst: Life sentence for being guilty of one murder and three rapes 24 years ago
articles.summary: Life sentence for being guilty of one murder and three rapes 24 years ago
articles.body:
The United States Justice Department has found Miguel Ángel Urbano Vázquez, a 50-year-old Mexican citizen, guilty of murdering and raping Sharon Van Gilder in Tacoma and committing three other rapes in Lincoln in 2002.

The criminal committed several of his sexual assaults in a workshop in the company of other individuals, and will receive a life sentence without the possibility of parole, according to U.S. media reports. He was convicted by a jury of first-degree aggravated murder, two counts of first-degree rape with a deadly weapon, and one count of second-degree rape.

Urbano Vázquez's modus operandi was similar in all his crimes. He targeted women addicted to alcohol or drugs, or those who were in a vulnerable situation, in order to abuse them.

Sharon Van Gilder, 39, was found dead in March 2002 in a ditch after being raped and murdered by Urbano Vázquez, whose DNA was found on the body. He also brutally abused three other women over a span of barely half a year. After being extradited to Mexico, the criminal finally faced U.S. justice to answer for his crimes, which had gone unsolved for many years.

Finally, an FBI investigation made it possible to prove that all the cases had been committed by the same serial rapist. It did so thanks to the comparison of DNA evidence that placed Urbano Vázquez at the crime scene and at the scenes of the three rapes. In 2023, he was arrested near Mexico City and placed at the disposal of the courts to be extradited to the United States.

"I feel that justice has been done and that he can no longer hurt anyone else," declared a relative of Van Gilder present in court.

articles.title: What are Costco's new coffee machines and kitchen items you can get now?
articles.standfirst: The retailer has added two very different coffee makers to its kitchen lineup
articles.summary: The retailer has added two very different coffee makers to its kitchen lineup
articles.body:
Making coffee at home has become increasingly sophisticated, and Costco is giving shoppers two very different options for upgrading their morning routine without sacrificing convenience.

The warehouse retailer has added the De'Longhi Magnifica Plus Fully Automatic Espresso Machine and SimplyGood Plastic Free Blooming Coffee Maker to its selection of kitchen appliances, with both featuring among notable Costco kitchen products for 2026.

Although both machines are designed to simplify coffee preparation, their prices and capabilities reflect fundamentally different approaches to brewing, making the choice largely dependent on customers' preferences.

The SimplyGood model costs approximately $300 and concentrates on producing traditional drip coffee, while the De'Longhi Magnifica Plus , priced around $1,000, offers a considerably more sophisticated experience.

The difference goes beyond the price tag, with one machine emphasizing brewing quality and materials while the other attempts to recreate the variety of drinks available at a professional coffee shop.

What are Costco's new coffee machines and how much do they cost?

The SimplyGood Plastic Free Blooming Coffee Maker is designed for customers who prefer straightforward preparation without unnecessary settings or complicated maintenance.

Its construction incorporates stainless steel, borosilicate glass and silicone, helping prevent plastic and aluminum from coming into contact with the water used for brewing.

The machine holds 40 ounces and can prepare eight cups in approximately six minutes, maintaining water temperatures between 195 and 205 degrees Fahrenheit.

One of its distinguishing features is an optional blooming cycle, which briefly wets coffee grounds before brewing to release trapped gases and promote more consistent extraction.

Customer feedback has been encouraging, with one Costco reviewer reporting "a substantial difference in taste" because of the machine's glass and stainless steel components.

The De'Longhi Magnifica Plus takes a different approach, providing 18 automated recipes that include espresso, cappuccino, Americano, flat white and iced coffee.

Its integrated conical burr grinder offers 13 settings, while the LatteCrema milk system allows users to customize the texture of foam for different beverages.

Customers can also choose between four drink sizes and five intensity settings, making the machine particularly attractive to households with different coffee preferences.

What other Costco kitchen items are worth looking at?

Beyond its coffee machines, Costco continues to expand its selection of convenient breakfast products designed for customers seeking quick meals without extensive preparation.

Among the options are Kirkland Signature Uncured Bacon and Gouda Egg Bites , which have attracted favorable customer feedback for their creamy texture and smoky flavor.

Shoppers can also find Veggies Made Great Broccoli Cheddar Breakfast Potato Bakes , sold in packs of 18 and prepared using potatoes, egg whites, vegetables and cheese.

Another option is Chef Hak's Breakfast Potatoes with Chicken Sausage , a fully cooked combination of roasted potatoes, peppers, onions and seasoned sausage.

These products provide alternatives to traditional breakfast preparation, although availability and pricing can vary between Costco warehouses and online listings.

Ultimately, the retailer's two coffee machines serve distinct audiences, with SimplyGood appealing to traditional coffee drinkers and De'Longhi offering greater versatility for those seeking cafe-style drinks at home.

articles.title: In 5700 BC, a volcano in the United States erupted and collapsed: this is how the country’s deepest lake was born, with an almost unreal blue
articles.standfirst: Crater Lake hides a log that has been floating upright for more than a century
articles.summary: Crater Lake hides a log that has been floating upright for more than a century
articles.body:
About 7,700 years ago, a mountain in the western United States blew apart . From that catastrophe emerged one of the most spectacular landscapes on the planet: a lake of such an intense blue that it seems unreal and that today holds the record for being the deepest in the country.

It is called Crater Lake , or Crater Lake, and it is located in the state of Oregon , within the national park that bears its name. Its origin lies in Mount Mazama , a volcano in the Cascade Range that underwent such a violent eruption that it ended up collapsing in on itself.

As the magma chamber emptied, the volcano's summit collapsed , leaving a huge hole, what geologists call a caldera. Over the centuries, rain and melted snow gradually filled it until it formed a lake about 594 meters deep.

The secret of its color is that no river or stream flows into it. The water only comes from the sky and only leaves through evaporation or by filtering into the ground, so it barely carries any sediments. That purity, combined with its enormous depth, gives it that striking blue color.

In the middle of the lake rises Wizard Island , the summit of a small volcano formed in later eruptions, which rises about 230 meters above the water. But visitors’ favorite curiosity is another: the "Old Man of the Lake" , a tree trunk that has been floating upright for more than a hundred years . The very cold water has helped preserve it.

For the Klamath , one of the area's Native tribes , the lake was a sacred place. One of their legends tells of two chiefs who clashed in a battle that destroyed the mountain, a story that some believe was inspired by the eruption itself.

The park, established in 1902 , now offers hiking trails, viewpoints, and boat tours in summer.

articles.title: Powerball Winning Numbers: Results of Wednesday, November 4 drawing for the $835 Million jackpot
articles.standfirst: Wednesday's drawing offers a cash option of $357.9 million after a Delaware ticket claimed the biggest prize in Monday's results
articles.summary: Wednesday's drawing offers a cash option of $357.9 million after a Delaware ticket claimed the biggest prize in Monday's results
articles.body:
The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $835 million for Wednesday, November 4, putting another enormous lottery prize within reach after Monday's drawing failed to produce a winner.

Players across the United States will be hoping to match all six numbers when the next drawing takes place at 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time, with the jackpot offering a lump-sum cash option of $357.9 million before taxes.

The prize increased after nobody matched the five white balls and red Powerball on Monday, November 2, extending a run of drawings without a grand prize winner.

Although the jackpot remained unclaimed, one ticket purchased in Delaware matched all five white balls to win $1 million, the largest prize awarded during Monday's drawing.

articles.title: You have to see Bob Dylan’s hoodie-clad Vatican meeting with Pope Leo to believe it
articles.standfirst: The legendary singer-songwriter swapped the stage for the Apostolic Palace, arriving in his trademark black hooded sweatshirt
articles.summary: The legendary singer-songwriter swapped the stage for the Apostolic Palace, arriving in his trademark black hooded sweatshirt
articles.body:
Bob Dylan has enjoyed some extraordinary encounters throughout his remarkable career, but his latest appearance might be among the most unusual as the 85-year-old music legend visited Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican on Wednesday, November 4, during a break from his Italian tour. Photographs of the meeting revealing an unmistakably casual outfit as rather than dressing for the occasion in a traditional suit, Dylan opted for a black hoodie, pulling the hood over his head as he sat alongside the leader of the Catholic Church .

The distinctive appearance quickly attracted attention after Vatican Media released photographs of the encounter as the private audience took place at the Apostolic Palace , where the two Americans exchanged greetings and enjoyed a brief conversation. According to the Vatican , the meeting included a few lighthearted exchanges, although the details of their discussion were not made public and there was also an exchange of rather personal gifts as Pope Leo presented Dylan with a rosary, while the singer-songwriter handed the pontiff a copy of his autobiography, Chronicles: Volume One . The meeting was arranged with the assistance of Jesuit priest Antonio Spadaro , who accompanied Dylan alongside Andrea Monda , editor of the Vatican newspaper L'Osservatore Romano . Spadaro subsequently described the experience as an emotional and historic encounter.

Why Pope Leo and Bob Dylan have more in common than expected

Although their respective careers have taken very different paths, the meeting had a connection beyond their shared American backgrounds. Leo has previously demonstrated an appreciation for Dylan 's songwriting, even referencing one of his lesser-known compositions in a publication earlier this year. In July 2026, the pontiff quoted Dylan 's unpublished 1963 protest song, Go Away You Bomb , in the preface to his book Disarmed and Disarming: Peace Is a Gift . The composition addresses the dangers of nuclear weapons and the responsibility of humanity for creating them. Leo used the lyrics to reinforce his opposition to the global arms race and the threat posed by nuclear escalation and among the words he referenced was Dylan 's line: "I hate you cause yer man-made and man-owned, an' man-handled." The connection also extends to his musical references to St. Augustine , whose teachings have profoundly influenced Leo 's spirituality and the Augustinian religious order to which he belongs. He then released I Dreamed I Saw St. Augustine on his 1967 album John Wesley Harding . This was not the singer's first encounter with a sitting pope as in 1997, he performed before Pope John Paul II and approximately 300,000 young people during the National Eucharistic Congress in Bologna, Italy. He performed three songs, including Knockin' on Heaven's Door , before greeting the pontiff and John Paul II subsequently referenced Dylan 's Blowin' in the Wind during his address to the audience. Born Robert Allen Zimmerman in Duluth, Minnesota , Dylan was raised in a Jewish family before undergoing a significant religious transformation towards the end of the 1970s as his Christian faith became a major influence on his music, particularly through albums including Slow Train Coming , Saved and Shot of Love . The transition surprised some longtime fans, although religious themes have remained present throughout his extensive catalogue, since, Dylan has become increasingly private about his beliefs in recent years making this a rare display for fans of the legend.

articles.title: Older man allegedly slaps teenage political activist during heated confrontation at New Hampshire polling place
articles.summary: An 18-year-old Turning Point Action volunteer was slapped during a confrontation outside the Woodland Heights polling location in Laconia, New Hampshire, on November 3, 2026, during the U.S. midterm elections.
articles.body:
An 18-year-old Turning Point Action volunteer was slapped during a confrontation outside the Woodland Heights polling location in Laconia, New Hampshire, on November 3, 2026, during the U.S. midterm elections.

Video shows an older man angrily arguing with the teenager, shouting profanities and raising his middle finger before striking him across the face with the back of his hand. The volunteer did not physically retaliate.

According to police, the confrontation began after the man approached the volunteer's booth and the two engaged in a political discussion. The argument escalated, although the footage does not show the entire exchange.

Police identified the suspect as Stephen Redic, 70, of Laconia. He was arrested on November 4 and charged with misdemeanor simple assault and disorderly conduct. His arraignment is scheduled for December 10.

Local officials and representatives of both major political parties condemned the incident.

articles.title: Social Security paperless COLA deadline: When is the last day this month to apply for paperless notice?
articles.standfirst: Social Security beneficiaries have until November 18, 2026, to create an online account and select paperless notices if they want early access to their personalised 2027 cost-of-living adjustment information
articles.summary: Social Security beneficiaries have until November 18, 2026, to create an online account and select paperless notices if they want early access to their personalised 2027 cost-of-living adjustment information
articles.body:
Millions of Americans waiting to find out how much their Social Security payments will increase next year have an important date to remember this month.

The Social Security Administration (SSA) has set November 18 as the deadline for beneficiaries who want to receive their 2027 COLA notice online rather than waiting for a letter through the post.

The deadline is approaching, meaning anyone who has not yet created a personal my Social Security account or enrolled in paperless communications should consider completing the process before November 18.

The SSA confirmed the date in its October 14 announcement, which revealed a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2027.

Those who complete the registration and select digital notices in time will be able to access their personalised benefit information online from late November, potentially up to three weeks before receiving the equivalent paper notification.

Importantly, November 18 is not the deadline to receive the COLA itself or to apply for Social Security benefits. It is specifically the cutoff for beneficiaries who want early online access to their annual adjustment notice.

People who do not register for paperless communications will still receive their information. The SSA has confirmed that paper notices will be delivered during December.

How to register for paperless Social Security notices

Beneficiaries who have not previously created an online account can visit the official SSA website at ssa.gov/myaccount to begin the process.

After creating an account, users should access their profile and notification preferences, where they can select the paperless communications option. The agency's instructions require users to switch the setting on, review the authorisation agreement and confirm their selection.

People who already have a my Social Security account should also check their preferences to make sure they are enrolled in paperless notices. Simply having an account does not necessarily mean that someone has selected digital delivery.

The SSA's online Message Center provides a secure location for receiving important documents, including annual COLA notifications. Users can also choose to receive email or text alerts when a new message becomes available.

The agency says the simplified, one-page notice will provide personalised information, including the exact amount of an individual's new benefit and any applicable deductions.

How much will Social Security payments increase in 2027?

The deadline comes after the SSA confirmed that benefits will increase by 3.6% next year, providing a boost to approximately 76 million Americans receiving Social Security and Supplemental Security Income (SSI).

According to the agency, the average retirement benefit will increase by approximately $75 per month. However, the actual amount individuals receive will depend on their existing benefit payment.

Nearly 72 million Social Security beneficiaries will begin receiving the higher payments in January 2027. Meanwhile, approximately 7.3 million SSI recipients will see their increased payments begin on December 31, 2026. Some Americans receive both types of assistance.

The COLA is designed to help benefits keep pace with rising living costs and is calculated using changes in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers.

For beneficiaries enrolled in Medicare , the online notice will also help them understand their updated payment after relevant deductions. Information about Medicare's 2027 changes will be available separately through Medicare.gov.

Those who miss the November 18 deadline will not lose their COLA increase or their right to receive the information. They will simply have to wait for the paper notification, which the SSA says will arrive in December.

With the deadline now less than two weeks away, beneficiaries who prefer digital access should make sure their accounts and communication preferences are correctly set up before November 18.

articles.title: Ernest Hemingway, American short story writer: "The world is worth fighting for, though leaving it brings sorrow... Dying is simple, but survivors suffer immensely"
articles.standfirst: The celebrated author explored the contradictions of human existence in his writing, reflecting on the beauty of life, the inevitability of death and the lasting pain experienced by those left behind
articles.summary: The celebrated author explored the contradictions of human existence in his writing, reflecting on the beauty of life, the inevitability of death and the lasting pain experienced by those left behind
articles.body:
E rnest Hemingway remains one of the most influential American writers of the 20th century, remembered for his distinctive prose, powerful short stories and novels that examined courage, love, conflict and loss.

Among the quotations associated with his work is a reflection on the value of life and the difficulty of accepting its end.

The words capture a central tension in Hemingway's writing: even in a world marked by violence and suffering, there are reasons to appreciate existence and resist giving up on it.

The original passage appears in his 1940 novel For Whom the Bell Tolls, although the version frequently shared online is often shortened.

The complete quotation reads: "If we win here we will win everywhere. The world is a fine place and worth the fighting for and I hate very much to leave it."

It is spoken by Robert Jordan , an American volunteer fighting alongside Republican forces during the Spanish Civil War.

The character's experiences place him in a situation where personal sacrifice, loyalty and the possibility of death become increasingly difficult to separate.

The novel follows Jordan as he joins a group of guerrilla fighters and receives a mission to destroy a bridge ahead of a military offensive.

As the operation approaches, he develops relationships with the people around him, particularly Maria, while confronting the consequences of the conflict.

Hemingway's words are powerful because they do not present life as perfect. Instead, they recognise that the world can be cruel while still containing things worth protecting. The character's reluctance to leave it gives the passage its emotional weight.

The quotation also reflects the author's ability to communicate complicated feelings through relatively straightforward language.

Rather than relying on elaborate philosophical explanations, Hemingway allows the character's circumstances and personal reflections to carry the meaning.

Hemingway's writing explored the relationship between life, death and loss

Death was a recurring subject throughout Hemingway's literary career. His experiences as a journalist and war correspondent, alongside his involvement in the First World War, helped shape his understanding of violence and the fragility of human life.

Born in Oak Park, Illinois, in 1899, Hemingway began his professional writing career in a newspaper office in Kansas City.

After the United States entered the First World War, he volunteered as an ambulance driver with the Italian army. He was seriously wounded in 1918 and spent considerable time recovering in hospital.

Those experiences influenced the subjects he returned to throughout his fiction. His novels frequently place ordinary people in extraordinary circumstances, forcing them to confront fear, suffering and decisions that can have irreversible consequences.

Works such as A Farewell to Arms, The Sun Also Rises and The Old Man and the Sea established his reputation as a writer capable of exploring emotional complexity through economical prose.

His interest in the human response to death is also examined in the PBS documentary project Hemingway . Scholars discussing his work explain how the presence of mortality shapes the decisions and personal codes of his characters.

That perspective helps explain why the passage from For Whom the Bell Tolls continues to resonate. It is not simply an observation about the end of life; it is also an acknowledgement of everything that makes existence meaningful.

Hemingway received the Pulitzer Prize in 1953 for The Old Man and the Sea and the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954. The Nobel committee recognized his mastery of narrative and the influence of his writing on contemporary literature.

He died on July 2, 1961, in Ketchum, Idaho, aged 61. His death by suicide followed years of serious personal difficulties and declining health, leaving a profound impact on his family.

More than six decades later, Hemingway's writing continues to attract readers because it addresses experiences that remain universally recognisable.

His characters confront uncertainty, grief and mortality, but they also find reasons to love, persevere and defend what matters to them.

The message behind his famous passage is therefore not that life is free from suffering. It is that its beauty and significance can remain visible even when the world offers painful reasons to turn away.

articles.title: Alaska Permanent Fund Status: How to know if you get the $1,200 payment this month?
articles.standfirst: Alaska residents waiting for their 2026 Permanent Fund Dividend have another opportunity to receive their money in November
articles.summary: Alaska residents waiting for their 2026 Permanent Fund Dividend have another opportunity to receive their money in November
articles.body:
Thousands of Alaskans are monitoring their Permanent Fund Dividend (PFD) applications as another payment date approaches.

The 2026 payment is worth $1,200 per eligible resident, combining a $1,000 dividend with an additional $200 energy relief payment. However, not everyone will receive the money at the same time.

The next scheduled distribution is November 19, 2026. To qualify for this payment round, applications must display the status "Eligible-Not Paid" by November 11.

This means submitting an application alone is not enough. The Alaska Department of Revenue must first confirm that the applicant meets the requirements and approve the payment.

Residents who have already received their 2026 dividend will not receive another $1,200. The November distribution is intended for eligible applicants who are still waiting for their money.

How to check your Alaska Permanent Fund application status

The simplest way to establish whether you are included in the November payment is through the state's official myPFD portal.

Residents can visit myPFD and sign in to review their application. The status to look for is "Eligible-Not Paid", which indicates that the application has been approved but the money has not yet been distributed.

If this status appears by November 11, the applicant should be included in the November 19 payment.

Anyone whose application is still being reviewed should continue checking for updates. The November payment is not guaranteed if the required status has not been reached by the deadline.

It is also important to ensure that personal information, particularly mailing addresses, is correct. Residents who have moved should update their details through the portal to avoid problems receiving a payment by post.

Who qualifies for the $1,200 payment?

The dividend is not automatically available to everyone living in Alaska. Applicants must satisfy the state's residency and other eligibility requirements.

For the 2026 payment, residents generally must have lived in Alaska throughout 2025 and intend to remain there indefinitely. They must also meet rules concerning absences from the state and must not have claimed residency elsewhere during the relevant period.

Applicants who spent more than 180 days outside Alaska must have been away for an allowable reason. They must also have been physically present in the state for at least 72 consecutive hours during 2024 or 2025.

Certain criminal convictions and periods of incarceration can also affect eligibility.

Importantly, the application period for the 2026 dividend has already closed. The November distribution concerns applications that have already been submitted and subsequently approved.

What if you miss the November payment?

Residents who do not qualify for the November round have another opportunity before the end of the year.

The next scheduled distribution is December 17, 2026. To be included, applications must reach "Eligible-Not Paid" status by December 9.

For anyone still waiting, regularly checking myPFD is the most reliable way to follow progress and establish when the money should arrive.

The $1,200 payment represents an important annual benefit for eligible Alaskans, but the distribution schedule depends on application processing.

Residents should use the official myPFD portal to check their individual status and consult the Alaska Department of Revenue for further information.

articles.title: Why did the stock market crash today and will it bounce back?
articles.standfirst: The Nasdaq, S&P 500, and Dow Jones all plummeted on Thursday, November 5.
articles.summary: The Nasdaq, S&P 500, and Dow Jones all plummeted on Thursday, November 5.
articles.body:
By this point, no one should be surprised when the stock market has a big fluctuation. That's been the name of the game for a long time now. But Thursday, November 5 was a whole different ballgame, as practically everything went down, and went down big .

At one point on Thursday, around $2.5 trillion in market cap was erased as the Nadaq, S&P 500, and Dow Jones all plummeted . This comes after the stock market saw a nice bump on Wednesday. That initial wave of optimism was completely wiped away on Thursday, and there's a very specific reason for it.

Many stock traders are worried that Democrats could regulate and restrict tech companies

When the stock market rose following Tuesday's midterm elections, it appeared to signal relief among traders that Democrats controlling the House and Senate would lead to more stability for the stock market. Instead, it seems that traders are actually becoming a bit fearful of a Democrat-run House and Senate .

What appears to be driving the massive sell-off on Thursday are worries that a Democratic congress could potentially increase regulation and restrictions when it comes to data centers . Many tech companies saw their stock prices rise meteorically over the past year or so, ever since the advent of AI and data centers.

If there are more regulations around building and maintaining the already existing data centers and potential new ones, that could very well lead to financial losses for a lot of the aforementioned companies . That's all speculation at this point in time, though. Following a true panic on Thursday morning, the stock market began rebounding at least slightly as the day went on .
